NaraUSD mint pulls supported collateral from msg.sender and mints only to msg.sender through MCT. Redemption burns caller NaraUSD and pays caller selected collateral; allowQueue=false reverts if liquidity is insufficient. Native collateral decimals are normalized to 18; division truncates. Mutable percentage/minimum fees, minimum amounts and per-block limits apply; no caller min-output/deadline parameter exists.

Queued redemption locks caller NaraUSD in the redeem silo; one request per address, NOT a FIFO queue despite primary documentation describing ordered service. Manager can complete opportunistically; caller tryCompleteRedeem can complete own request if liquidity/caps permit. Completion burns escrow and pays caller at current fees; it does not recheck Keyring expiry. Asset removal can block completion. cancelRedeem returns escrow subject to pause/blacklist; updateRedemptionRequest funds/refunds the difference without changing asset. No payout date is guaranteed.

NaraUSD+ deposit/mint pulls caller NaraUSD and issues shares to receiver; 18-decimal underlying/shares, balance-minus-unvested-rewards ERC4626 exchange rate with virtual offsets. Deposit floors shares; mint rounds required assets up. NAV/income originates from offchain payment-financing operations and maker/reviewer/executor controls, not autonomous proof of portfolio value; insurance then staked shares absorb losses, and principal can be lost.

NaraUSD+ cooldown was 604800 seconds (7 days) and both proxies paused=false at the observed block, not continuing availability. Direct withdraw/redeem is structurally disabled while cooldown is nonzero and excluded. cooldownAssets rounds shares up; cooldownShares locks exact caller shares. Both transfer shares into silo and adding to an existing cooldown resets unlock for ALL locked shares. Assets returned by preview are not a fixed future entitlement; shares continue rate exposure until unstake burns at claim-time rate to receiver. cancelCooldown returns locked shares.

Queue and cooldown ledgers explicitly narrow amounts to uint152; callers must keep queued/updated/aggregate locked share amounts within that range. Minimum-share invariants can prevent dust exits. unstake has no top-level pause modifier but calls _withdraw, which enforces pause/blacklists/nonzero/minimum shares. No silo administrative or direct transfer method is admitted.

Primary docs target redemption within 7 days but mention pressure up to roughly 90 days; these are not contract-enforced completion promises. Source and ABI review proves none of the portfolio, backing, yield or solvency claims.

bond is payable: only caller msg.value ETH funds the purchase; it mints the specified nonzero bonder both CDT and the option NFT. Set both minimum entitlements and a deadline; owner-controlled BCF, NAV floor and debt ceiling affect new quotes.

Note USD/CDT/STRAT/esETH quantities use 18-decimal scales; native ETH is wei. Oracle price uses its configured scale. Integer divisions floor. Bond entitlement is NAV-plus-premium priced, esETH entitlement is capped at ETH paid, and can be zero underwater. No guaranteed parity, return or immediate redemption is asserted.

convert and convertPartial use an internally empty permit record whose deadline=0 skips permit entirely; no wallet authorization or new backend signing is introduced. Both require caller==ownerOf(tokenId), burn caller CDT under existing allowance and pay STRAT or esETH only to that owner. NFT operator approvals do not confer conversion authority. Partial conversion floors pro-rata outputs and decrements the note; full exercise burns it.

New notes are timelocked for 6.9 days and expire after 4.2*365 days. Pre-expiry conversion is unavailable during the timelock. redeemCdtForUsdNotional settles the entire remaining owned note only after expiry, burns caller CDT and the NFT, and applies minEthOut. Payout is esETH, not native ETH or stablecoin, and is pro-rata treasury value if underwater.

Conversions/redemptions depend on esETH balances and finite allowances from the holdings Safes, oracle, mint/burn authorizations and circuit breaker. Full dependency runtime/financial safety was not attested. Deployed redemption code transfers the note's remaining encumbered entitlement before payment but does NOT implement the documentation's separately claimed additional shortfall sweep; an insufficient unencumbered balance can revert.

sEARN stake pulls only caller EARN and mints a nontransferable 1:1 caller position. unstake burns only caller position and returns EARN, auto-claiming accrued USDS; claim pays only caller accrued USDS. These are financial staking/reward methods, not EARN market buy/sell helpers. Acquisition, approval and market exit are not supplied here.

sEARN reward batches blend into a value-weighted 28-day linear stream; integer reward-rate/per-share arithmetic floors and income depends on funding. No new yield is promised. Selected staking methods synchronise rewards internally. Native value must be zero for every selected method except bond.

functions.label: Wise Token createStake financial position operation
warnings: Static source/ABI metadata only; not an API-key grant, live availability or authorization, persistent runtime attestation, principal/backing/yield safety, funded execution or a complete workflow. Independent policies, grants, pauses and canonical calldata/value controls remain mandatory.

Ethereum original WiseToken regular staking only, counted once across Wise Token/Wise Finance; not StakeWise. Sourcify reports runtimeMatch=match and creationMatch=match, not exact_match, and no proxy. Modern official docs explicitly maintain regular staking and link this exact token/staking address. Advanced NFT staking, RWA strategies and Wise lending are not admitted.

createStake burns msg.sender WISE and records a caller-owned stake; endStake and scrapeInterest read only msg.sender stake IDs and mint back to that caller. WISE amounts have 18 decimals, minimum stake is 1,000,000 base units and lockDays range 1..15,330. Stake starts next protocol day. Referrer must differ from caller and have no deployed code; zero referrer is allowed. No wallet/operator/delegation permission is granted.

Early ending an already started, unmatured stake loses principal according to source floor(stakedAmount * (100 + floor(800 * (daysLeft-1) / max(lockDays-1,1))) / 1000), not the simplified remaining-time percentage in current docs. Before start or after maturity penalty is zero. Remaining principal plus accrued WISE rewards is minted to caller; principal is not collateral-backed protection.

Scraping interest before maturity reduces remaining staking and referrer shares and may reduce future earnings; zero scrapeDays means all calculated days. Positive scrapeDays are caller-selected and may revert if snapshots are unavailable. Reward/day/share arithmetic rounds down; day loops and snapshot catch-up can consume substantial gas. No bounded-gas success or advertised APY is assured.

createStakeWithETH spends msg.value using fixed Uniswap V2 WETH->WISE path and then stakes output credited to msg.sender. createStakeWithToken pulls caller token, approves the fixed router internally, swaps token->WETH->WISE and stakes output; this is a fixed financial conversion, not arbitrary calldata execution. Both hard-code minimum swap output=1 and deadline=block.timestamp+2 hours, with no caller slippage minimum or custom deadline. Adverse execution/MEV risk is material. Only createStakeWithETH is payable; all other admitted methods require zero native value.

Referrer claims mint only caller-owned referral-link rewards. Existing critical-mass eligibility, underlying stake state and snapshot accounting apply; processDays bounds processing only for ended/mature stakes, while active stakes use elapsed days. Bulk stake and referral methods are fixed loops, not multicall; matched array lengths, balances, and practical gas bounds are caller responsibility and one revert reverts the whole call.

Accrual depends on configured Uniswap pair reserves, hard-coded liquidity guard 0x9c306cad86550ec80d77668c0a8bee6eb34684b6 and fixed router/factory/token behavior. Liquidity-guard rates can reallocate inflation. These dependency deployments and current balances are not independently attested. No pause/read state or fee-free execution guarantee is asserted.

Ethereum PWN Simple Loan v1.3 at 0x719a69d0dc67bd3aa7648d4694081b3c87952797 only. Official pinned deployment manifest and current public product bind the maintained P2P loan product. Deployed source is exact_match for runtime/creation and proxyResolution.isProxy=false; no root proxy or successor alias is substituted. This does not independently attest mutable configuration or dependency runtimes.

repayLOAN pulls the exact recorded-credit repayment amount from msg.sender, who may be the borrower or any voluntary payer. Collateral is returned only to the recorded borrower, never to an arbitrary payer-selected recipient. Loan must be running and repayment must occur strictly before defaultTimestamp. Fee-on-transfer/rebasing or unsupported token balance behavior can revert exact-balance checks. Credit amounts use each loan token's own base units, with no universal decimals.

Repayment is principal plus fixed interest plus any accruing interest, measured in whole elapsed minutes and rounded down by Math.mulDiv. APR units have two decimals; source denominator is 100*100*525600. Repayment fixes accrued interest and zeroes accruing APR. No caller max repayment input, slippage cap or separate repayment fee is provided; time-sensitive amount and token allowance must already be adequate.

After returning collateral, repayment attempts self-only automatic settlement to the original lender or recorded original funding pool through a registered config adapter. Failure is caught so a lender cannot block borrower repayment; the loan remains repaid and claimable rather than guaranteeing immediate lender receipt. Config/pool adapters, loan NFT ownership, token behavior and dependency upgrades remain material unverified dependencies.

claimLOAN is restricted to the current LOAN NFT holder. It burns the LOAN NFT and deletes position data before transferring either recorded repayment credit (repaid loan) or recorded collateral (running loan at/after default). This is financial position settlement, not a bare transfer helper. Default losses and collateral value risk remain with counterparties; no oracle liquidation or principal protection is promised.

makeExtensionProposal records a hash only when extension.proposer==msg.sender. extendLOAN accepts only borrower/current loan owner as caller and requires the opposite party as proposer; fixed EIP712 domain binds chain, root contract, version and all extension fields. Existing onchain proposal or counterparty EOA/EIP1271 proof can authorize these fixed financial terms. signature bytes are proof, not executable calldata or backend wallet/permit/role authority; no new typed-data signing capability is added.

Extensions add 1..90 days to the original default timestamp, not to current time. Repaid/nonexistent loans cannot extend; source does not require the prior default timestamp to be in the future, so a still-unclaimed defaulted loan may extend and may remain defaulted if new maturity is still past. Proposal expiration and usable nonce/nonce-space are checked and nonce revoked. Nonzero compensation token+amount pulls borrower-funded compensation to current loan holder using existing allowance, even when the loan holder submits acceptance of borrower proposal. All admitted methods are nonpayable and require zero native value.

Only repayment, claim and extension proposal/acceptance are admitted. Loan origination/refinancing proposal dispatcher, proposal creation contracts, nonce authorization, generic callbacks, NFT approvals/transfers and governance/configuration are not capabilities here; no full loan-origination workflow is promised. Independent full financial/dependency safety attestation is not an admission prerequisite.

Direct implementation() calls resolved Ethereum to 0x0f1adffffd84749e816066348d4c1256d285965f and Base to 0x9bc729668f015e6059e8efeeb2145b08f94e1eff. Root and implementations have exact_match creation/runtime records. Admin can replace implementations, comptroller, rate model, reserves and whitelist.

USDC has 6 decimals and caUSDC 8. mint pulls msg.sender approved underlying, measures actual received balance delta and floors caTokens at current exchange rate; redeem burns caller caTokens and floors underlying output. redeemUnderlying requests underlying and floors caTokens consumed; there is no minimum-output, maximum-share-burn or deadline argument. Exchange rate/interest can move before execution.

borrow adds interest-indexed principal only to msg.sender and sends underlying to that same borrower; available cash and comptroller liquidity/market rules apply. repayBorrow pulls only caller funds and reduces caller own interest-accrued debt. uint256.max repays full current debt; ordinary overpayment can underflow and revert, not automatically cap/refund.

Financial entrypoints accrue interest, use comptroller permission hooks and may revert; ABI uint256 success result is NO_ERROR=0 in the reviewed implementation, not a successful-execution guarantee. Transfer, approval, seize, liquidation, behalf repayment, generic delegation, reserve donation and admin/upgrade methods are excluded. Controller membership/enterMarkets and approvals are not granted here; no complete collateral-onboarding workflow is promised.

Both caUSDC markets were listed with mintGuardianPaused=false and borrowGuardianPaused=false, and whitelist()=zero at the point-in-time calls. A future configured active whitelist can restrict mint; borrowing and redemption remain subject to mutable controller/oracle/collateral state. Oracle, controller implementation, token and rate-model independent runtime/safety attestations are not established.

buyEnabled and sellEnabled were each 1 on all reviewed roots, and collateral Join live flags were 1 at observation. Governance can change these settings and fees. warnings: Static deployment/source/ABI metadata only; not live authorization, persistent runtime attestation, backing, liquidity, financial safety, successful execution or a complete workflow. Independent grants, pauses, policies and canonical calldata/value controls remain mandatory; nonpayable calls require zero native value.

Ethereum Vectis UltraX Arb V2 vault only, with immutable USDC asset and strategy address. Etherscan binds its full source/ABI by Similar Match to 0x0963c0f17d77e336ff75ed36c27d3a1522847615; this is not exact_match and root Sourcify record is absent. Root is a directly deployed AccountableAsyncRedeemVault, not a proxy. Its fixed strategy is an upgradeable AccountableYield proxy; external dependency behavior remains mutable and is not a safety assurance.

At Ethereum block 26260475, permissionLevel=0, depositGateway=zero, loanState=3 (OngoingDynamic), strategy.paused=false. These observations permit ordinary plain canonical calldata, not a continuing availability promise. KYC appended authorization/signature suffixes and backend typed-data signing are not admitted. Existing operator approvals can satisfy ownership/controller checks, but setOperator and all role/approval functions are excluded; prefer caller-owned/controller positions.

USDC assets and VUXA shares use 6 decimals. deposit floors output shares at strategy-returned NAV; mint rounds required assets up. The two-argument forms fund from msg.sender; three-argument forms pull from controller only when caller is controller or its already-approved operator. Receiver/controller fields are fixed financial recipients, not arbitrary-call execution. There is no caller minimum-output, maximum-input or deadline parameter; NAV and fees may change before inclusion.

RequestRedeem checks owner and controller rights, moves owner VUXA shares into vault escrow and either reserves liquidity immediately (requestId=0) or aggregates the controller pending request into the withdrawal queue. Pending queue requests may be partially fulfilled by the strategy at future NAV; no settlement date, principal protection or immediate liquidity is guaranteed. cancelRedeemRequest returns all still-pending controller shares to receiver if strategy permits; already-claimable shares remain separate.

redeem and withdraw claim only controller assigned fulfilled shares/assets, not arbitrary free pool balances. Redeem floors assets and conservatively decrements recorded asset limit with ceiling rounding; withdraw floors burned shares and decrements share entitlement conservatively using ceiling rounding. Both burn escrowed shares and transfer fixed USDC to receiver; prior fulfillment is required. Minimum vault amount is 10000 raw units; current product config reports minDeposit=100000000 raw USDC and minRedeem=100000000 raw shares, with mutable capacity and stale-NAV gates.

Current primary product/config states 2% annual management fee and 20% performance fee, zero establishment fee. Strategy accrues management/performance charges through dilutive fee-share minting with a high-water mark; NAV includes accrual effects. Manager, borrower, exchange custody, fee manager, NAV publishing and default/loss handling affect value. Assets support managed strategies across Binance/Hyperliquid/OKX with Ceffu/Cobo custody; market-neutral marketing is not a risk-free or principal guarantee. No custody, borrower repayment, fee-manager, oracle or other dependency safety attestation is claimed.

warnings: Static deployment/source/ABI metadata only; no live authorization, persistent runtime attestation, backing, liquidity, financial safety, successful execution or complete workflow assurance. Independent grants, policy, pauses and canonical calldata/value controls remain mandatory.

Ethereum nonproxy SatoSwapRouter buy/sell only. Current official frontend selects ETH/SATO fee 3000, tickSpacing 60, hook 0x0000f07d2b5f1ddf3244b8780f972f306efd2888 through immutable Uniswap v4 PoolManager 0x000000000004444c5dc75cb358380d2e3de08a90. Router accepts a PoolKey and does NOT itself force this key; these are typed financial pool/asset/hook fields, not arbitrary executable bytes. Other pool keys are not evidence of SATO curve behavior.

Buy spends msg.value in native ETH wei; sell pulls satoIn from msg.sender under an already-existing token allowance and requires zero native value. Recipient receives output; swapper is caller-supplied cooldown identity, not payer authorization. Caller must supply the intended identity; the contract does not enforce swapper=caller or recipient. No approvals, permits, hook callbacks or opaque unlockCallback calls admitted.

Curve SATO uses 18 decimals; ETH uses wei. Hook charges floor(amount*30/10000), 0.3%, on ETH input or gross ETH redemption. Fees accrue in hook with no withdrawal method. PRBMath fixed-point exp/log, floor ratios and fair-supply correction create rounding and economic spread; not a fixed price or peg.

Exact input only: buy has 5 ETH per-call maximum. Neither router method provides minimum output or deadline; price movement and value loss are possible. Sell applies lastBuyBlock cooldown to supplied swapper and burns SATO against hook ETH inventory. No promised backing or payout; insufficient reserves or token/manager failure revert.

Hook forbids all LP additions; no LP deposit/withdrawal capabilities exist here. At the observed reads selfDeprecated=false and poolInitialized=true. Reaching 99% fair-supply threshold irreversibly disables future curve buys, including after later burns; not a current retirement finding. Genesis first-100-block entropy window is closed. No admin, pause or upgrade path in router/hook source; dependency runtime not independently attested.

Ethereum Brickken factory id 54 investor escrow only. Current getImplementation() and beacon implementation() both resolve to 0x4459432f1626cc4de0e0a004e74ff282ae9c4a6f. Beacon 0xe2f8f2910d923e660a4a526f7c08ef3ddd7a713d is effective because the EIP1967 implementation override slot is zero. getTokens(index,onBehalfOf) settles the recorded investor, not an arbitrary receiver: successful offering claims mint precisely that investor's recorded STO amount; rollback refunds precisely that investor's recorded payment-token amount. Any caller must already be whitelisted on the related token; this catalog neither creates KYC approval nor grants a role.

Ethereum current sHAKKA v2 0xb925863a15ebdeae1a638bf2b6fd00d4db897a62 and linked reward pool 0x735a80510536a9a18c8824f40dbc92824640c95a only. HAKKA and sHAKKA amounts use 18-decimal token base units. stake(to,amount,time) pulls only caller HAKKA, creates a lock owned by to and mints that owner transferable sHAKKA plus internal votingPower accounting. Voting-power accounting does not grant any governance transaction capability here.

Current observed staking model 0x3474b74139c192d0781812ca70cc410d19cb6a2d returns zero outside 30 minutes through 1461 days. Receipt conversion is floor(amount*rate/1e18), with time-dependent model checkpoints and selected lock term, not accrued HAKKA interest or ERC4626 NAV. Owner may replace the model; bounds/rates are not guaranteed to remain fixed.

restake acts only on callers vault index, may pull additional caller HAKKA, resets unlockTime to now+time and must extend the former unlock and produce at least the existing receipt amount. It can extend a lock without adding capital. It is not an early exit or a reward claim.

unstake acts only on callers vault after unlockTime; it burns callers sHAKKA and returns floor(receiptAmount*remainingVaultHAKKA/remainingVaultReceipts) HAKKA to the fixed payout recipient. Owning transferred sHAKKA alone does not transfer the original vault mapping; a lock owner who transferred/farmed receipts must recover enough to burn. No early-redemption bypass or guaranteed market value exists.

Reward-pool stake/stakeFor pull caller sHAKKA and credit the caller/named beneficiary internal reward stake; withdraw releases only callers recorded sHAKKA. stakeFor gifts the stake and reward rights to beneficiary. exit combines full own withdrawal and getReward; with zero staked balance it reverts due positive withdrawal requirement. No additional pool lock is present, but the original HAKKA vault maturity still applies.

getReward sends accrued HAKKA into VestingVault 0x51f12323820b3c0077864990d9e6ad9604238ed6 for caller, NOT liquid HAKKA to caller. Reward accounting is time-limited by periodFinish, integer floor rounding and mutable distributor funding; current primary farm displays 0.00% APR, so no positive emissions/yield promise. VestingVault withdrawal is not admitted here; a complete reward cashout workflow is not promised.

Stake/unstake/receipt-pool bodies deduct no explicit entry/exit fee, but lock duration, receipt conversion, funding and vesting can materially affect liquidity/value. HAKKA price, contract custody and dependency failure risks remain. Owner-only model/distribution/rescue methods, ERC20 approvals/transfers and authority management are excluded. Root rescue cannot extract HAKKA; pool rescue excludes HAKKA and its sHAKKA stake token. Model and reward-vesting dependencies are not a financial safety guarantee.

lockToken pulls caller-owned ERC20/LP tokens and records a time-locked internal deposit for the designated withdrawalAddress; actual credited amount is the vault token-balance increase, accommodating transfer fees but providing no minimum credited amount. Token amounts use native units. Withdrawal address is not checked nonzero by this body: an unusable recipient can strand the claim. Unlock time must be strictly in the future; no early withdrawal is provided.

lockNFT pulls only caller ERC721 tokenId, requires amount == 1 and future unlockTime, and records withdrawalAddress. Optional _mintNFT creates the protocol receipt NFT; it is not wallet/operator authorization, but adds dependency on the configured NFT contract. Standalone receipt mint and lock ownership transfers are not admitted. No arbitrary executable calldata, permit or backend signing is accepted.

Payable locks calculate native ETH fees through mutable estimator/USD-token settings and caller/token fee exemptions. Ordinary fee payment accepts up to 5% under quote; excess is refunded with a native call. Nonzero referrer cannot equal caller, requires configured discount and receives a configured fraction of the fee; referral and refund calls can fail. splitLock charges the ordinary non-referral fee. No fixed fee or refund success is promised.

extendLockDuration only extends an own unwithdrawn lock to a strictly later future timestamp. splitLock only divides an own ERC20 lock into two positive balances, with the new unlockTime no earlier than the original and same recorded withdrawal address. It cannot split a locked ERC721. If a receipt NFT exists, required current receipt ownership is checked in addition to the recorded withdrawal-address conditions.

withdrawTokens requires caller be the recorded withdrawal address, plus receipt-NFT ownership if minted, and waits until unlockTime. ERC20 withdrawals support positive partial amounts; full withdrawal clears the record and burns any receipt. For ERC721, _amount is ignored and the recorded tokenId is returned. Outputs go only to caller. Withdraw and extension do not have whenNotPaused; source guards are not assertions of current paused state.

collectUniswapV3LPFees requires caller be the recorded withdrawalAddress of an unwithdrawn NFT lock and invokes only the fixed collect tuple at that locked NFT contract, sending both fee assets to that same address with uint128 maximum amounts. There is no caller-supplied call payload; incompatible or malicious locked NFTs can revert or behave unexpectedly. Principal remains locked until maturity.

Proxy and owner powers are material: current implementation includes owner-only recoverAssets(user,newRecipient), which can reassign whole user deposit claims and burn receipts; ownership, fee configuration, pausing and upgrades remain mutable and are excluded. Marketing statements of noncustody do not override this source fact. The historical migration exploit is not admitted: current ABI has no migrate executor, and current primary pages explicitly offer ordinary new locks, splitting and partial claims, not recovery-only services.

lock and vestingLock pull exactly amount from msg.sender into a recorded financial lock, not shared-pool prefunding. Existing token allowance is required and none is granted here. Fee-on-transfer/rebasing transfers that fail the exact balance-delta check revert. owner/params.owner is the irrevocable initial beneficiary; source does not reject zero beneficiary, so a zero or unintended beneficiary can strand funds.

Amounts use each token native decimals; times and cycle use seconds, vesting fractions use basis points (10000 denominator). Plain locks require positive amount and future endTime. Vesting requires future tgeTime, positive tgeBps/cycleBps and sum <=10000; cycle must be positive for any vesting release, although source does not enforce that at creation. Integer-floor TGE/cycle releases can round to zero; do not assume eventual release of tiny amounts.

Fees are mutable by owner and selected through feeName; docs fee tables are not a live quote. LP detection uses fixed factory/token0/token1/getPair static calls. LP fee floors amount*lpFee/10000, transfers that LP fee to its pair and burns to mutable feeReceiver; only the remaining amount is locked. Native lock fee requires exact msg.value when positive and fee token is zero; token fee is separately pulled from caller. Otherwise use zero native value: unused msg.value has no refund path.

updateLock is caller-owner-only, requires positive additional caller-funded tokens, no previously unlocked amount, and a strictly later endTime also in the future. It charges the stored feeName again and increases amount net of LP fee; no relock-only shortcut is provided.

unlock is caller-owner-only and pays the recorded owner. A plain lock returns its full remaining recorded amount once mature; vesting returns all currently accrued tranches, caps at recorded amount, and debits unlocked/cumulative ledgers. No early cancellation, yield return, price guarantee, transfer authority, permit or ownership-management method is admitted. Token/pair behavior and mutable fee configuration remain external dependencies.

Own financial capital staking ledger, not an agent registry or bare MOR token helper. stake/withdraw/lockClaim are nonpayable and require zero native value. Current source overrides imprecise guide wording: Distributor.supply pulls stETH directly from the caller to Distributor and credits actual balance increase, including stETH share-rounding effects. Existing allowance must target Distributor, not merely DepositPool; no approval/permit is admitted. Configured strategy holds stETH or supplies supported assets to Aave; current stETH pool0 observed strategy NONE (0), with isExist=true and migration complete.

Stake requires positive amount and resulting own deposited balance >= mutable minimalStake. Zero claimLockEnd preserves an unexpired existing end or uses current time; an explicit end cannot reduce the prior end. New stake resets lastStake and claimLockStart, recomputes virtual stake and checkpoints rewards. Nonzero referrer affects financial reward accounting, is not an operator grant; zero preserves the existing referrer rather than removing it.

withdraw clamps requested amount to own deposited balance, asks Distributor to transfer principal directly to msg.sender, and credits the actual recipient balance delta. It requires the configured delay after lastStake, a positive actual amount, and remaining stake >= minimalStake or <10 token base units for stETH rounding dust. Full transaction reverts if later checks fail. It checkpoints rewards, updates referral/virtual stake and resets claimLockStart. No slippage minimum, guaranteed liquidity or loss reimbursement is provided.

lockClaim only extends the caller existing funded stake reward-claim lock to a strictly later future timestamp, checkpoints rewards and increases time-based virtual stake; it cannot withdraw, delegate or shorten a lock. Multipliers and emissions use integer-floor accounting and do not guarantee earnings. Observed pool0 exists/is public and migration is complete only at the captured block; pool timing, minimums, strategies, reward/oracle dependencies and upgrades remain mutable.

All MOR claim and referral-claim methods are deliberately excluded because current _claim paths call Distributor.sendMintMessage with native value, introducing cross-chain reward mint messaging. No bridge, backend signing, claim-sender/receiver authorization, owner migration, private-pool management, upgrade, arbitrary payload or token-transfer helper is admitted. Consequently this is not a complete MOR reward-claim workflow. Underlying yield is withdrawn to the configured L1 sender for protocol use, not paid to the depositor as stETH yield.

functions.label: HAI Cancel pending KITE withdrawal
warnings: Static deployment-bound source/ABI inventory only. No current runtime identity, balances, funding, backing, liquidity, execution, complete-workflow or financial-safety guarantee. Calls require zero native value and independent exact-function grants, pause and canonical-calldata controls.

Direct Optimism (10) KITE StakingManager, not GEB proxyActions or arbitrary execution. KITE is 0xf467C7d5a4A9C4687fFc7986aC6aD5A4c81E1404 and stKITE is 0xf632D72378D887e337C52Ff57FCd454f78881fc3, both app-configured 18-decimal units. stake(address,uint256) pulls caller KITE with manager allowance and credits/mints stKITE to the specified nonzero account; amounts must be positive.

initiateWithdrawal(uint256) removes caller active stake/reward participation immediately and creates or increases one pending withdrawal; adding to it resets its timestamp for the entire pending amount. It does not pay KITE or burn stKITE yet. cancelWithdrawal restores the entire pending amount to active stake and clears the request.

withdraw() claims the entire caller pending amount only after mutable cooldownPeriod, burns caller stKITE using burnFrom and pays KITE to caller. Requires sufficient stKITE balance AND allowance to the manager, in addition to the initial KITE deposit allowance. No arbitrary owner/recipient argument, partial final withdrawal or immediate-exit promise.

Constructor cooldown was 1209600 seconds (14 days); pinned frontend fallback config is 1814400 seconds (21 days). Neither establishes current onchain _params.cooldownPeriod. Source is authoritative: current mutable cooldown applies to pending withdrawals. The docs statement that users can unstake at any time does not establish immediate claimability.

getReward(address) may be triggered by anyone but pays the named account. getRewardAndForward(address,address) requires msg.sender == account and forwards only its reward tokens to the requested recipient; no arbitrary external target execution. Reward integral division floors, claims are capped by recorded remaining rewards, and inactive types are skipped. No minimum reward or deadline.

Stake, request/cancel and claims checkpoint configured reward pools; mint/burn of stKITE also checkpoints its configured manager. These fixed/configured dependencies can revert and prevent operations. Authorized accounts can add/deactivate reward pools, alter cooldown, rescue principal/rewards, and alter staking-token manager/transfer configuration. No current pool/token configuration or payout assurance.

Reviewed user methods have no KYC or role gate. Official site terms, currently linked by the app (published 2024-02-20), require adulthood, sophisticated use, applicable-law compliance and sanctions/jurisdiction eligibility, and prohibit credit-protocol site use from prohibited jurisdictions. functions.label: Tarot Deposit native USDC
warnings: Static source/ABI inventory only: no fresh runtime identity, funding, liquidity, execution success, complete workflow or financial-safety assurance. Exact-function grants, canonical calldata/value checks, pauses and independent controls still apply.

Only OP Mainnet native-USDC SupplyVaultV2 0x4ac8af23f3ef7ededb3dc45c091406aeee8de471 is admitted. Underlying is 6-decimal native USDC 0x0b2c639c533813f4aa9d7837caf62653d097ff85 and tUSDC shares also use 6 decimals. This is not Fantom legacy tUSDC, bridged USDC.e, a leveraged router, or an unrelated curator wrapper.

enter pulls positive USDC from caller with allowance to this vault and mints shares to caller. enterWithToken accepts only the fixed underlying or an owner-enabled registered Tarot borrowable, valuing the latter with its exchangeRate; it is not a caller-selected executor or arbitrary token swap. Tokens must not be taxed. Shares floor on conversion and there is no minimum-shares or deadline, including zero-share mint risk for small deposits.

leave burns caller shares and pays caller underlying after configured strategy deallocation, which can fail for insufficient cash or strategy authorization/configuration. Share value is recomputed after unwinding costs and may be lower. No share allowance/delegated owner, minimum output or deadline; positive output and sufficient cash are required. No queued claim or guaranteed withdrawal delay.

leaveInKind burns caller shares and sends proportional underlying AND every registered borrowable token, including disabled borrowables, to caller without attempting cash redemption. It is callable while paused, but that does not make retired deployments eligible. Per-token floors can produce dust/zero components; at least one payout is required. This admission does not separately admit redemption of the received borrowable tokens.

Initial constructor pauses the vault, but current explorer snapshot reports paused=false, native-USDC underlying and strategy 0x1753F90AcC5fF758Eb621F935ef0F99254289fb1; the current official app lists this exact OP vault without paused/deactivated flags. These observations are not persistent state guarantees. Underwater checkpoint accounting blocks deposits until restored even if global pause is false.

Fee accounting mints shares on gains above checkpoint to feeTo; initial feeBps=1000, owner may set 0..5000. Current explorer snapshot reported feeBps=1000 and feeTo=zero (fee mint skipped), not a permanent fee waiver. Owner controls pause, borrowable membership, fee recipient and strategy changes; strategy update requires a 2..30-day not-before window and 14-day grace. No user lockup is encoded in ordinary calls.

Ordinary entry/exit use configured strategy allocate/deallocate, not user opaque payloads. Source-bound current reported SupplyVaultStrategyV4 restricts these to authorized vaults and registered borrowables; its deallocation can revert INSUFFICIENT_CASH. Current strategy authorization and member-token behavior are unattested. Administrative reallocate(bytes), delegation/signatures, token approvals/transfers and accounting/quote maintenance stay unadmitted.

No user KYC/allowlist check appears in reviewed ordinary vault source; this does not establish jurisdictional eligibility, sanctions compliance or legal permission. All selected calls are nonpayable and require zero native value.

functions.label: Unwrap caller DAIx into DAI
warnings: Static deployment-bound source/ABI inventory only; no fresh runtime identity, execution, funding, balances, liquidity, complete-workflow or financial-safety assurance. Independent exact-function grants, pauses and canonical-calldata/value controls remain mandatory.

This admission is only the officially listed Optimism DAIx wrapper 0x7d342726b69c28d942ad8bfe6ac81b972349d524 over 18-decimal DAI 0xda10009cbd5d07dd0cecc66161fc93d7c9000da1. SuperToken quantities are 18-decimal units, not fiat amounts. Official tokenlist and explorer identify this exact wrapper and underlying; no arbitrary token factory, Host callAgreement or stream executor is admitted.

upgrade(amount) transfers underlying from msg.sender using allowance to this DAIx proxy, then mints DAIx to msg.sender atomically. downgrade(amount) burns caller DAIx and sends underlying to caller; downgradeTo(to,amount) burns caller DAIx and sends underlying to the chosen intended recipient. No delegated owner spending, share allowance or standalone prefunding is admitted.

Amount arguments are in 18-decimal SuperToken units. _toUnderlyingAmount rescales for underlying decimals, flooring when underlying has fewer decimals, but this DAI wrapper reports 18 underlying decimals so source conversion is equal raw units. Balance-delta checks reject input/output discrepancies at the wrapper; no exchange-rate/min-output or deadline argument exists. No market-value, backing or redemption-success guarantee follows.

Downgrade requires sufficient real-time available balance after ongoing agreements and deposits, not merely a historical ERC20 balance. The selected calls do not create, change or terminate streams and do not withdraw locked stream deposits. Source has no built-in redemption queue/wait in these bodies; configured dependencies and underlying liquidity may revert.

Selected functions pass empty userData/operatorData and disable the ERC777 send/receive hooks for wrapping/unwrapping. upgradeTo(address,uint256,bytes) is excluded because nonempty userData enables ERC777 recipient callbacks with opaque data; transfer/send/operator surfaces, callback registration, agreement internals and generic Host execution are not admitted.

Proxy implementation is source-service/explorer-reported 0x0742De30799351f892Dc7FaE8D76A265D6E772eA, independently source-verified exact_match. Explorer snapshot reports admin=zero (Host has admin privilege), Host=0x567c4B141ED61923967cA25Ef4906C8781069a10, and yieldBackend=zero. Admin/Host can upgrade implementation and configure a yield backend; a nonzero backend receives fixed-interface delegatecalls on wrapping/unwrapping and can affect/revert behavior. Point-in-time metadata is not a permanent configuration or fresh runtime identity assertion.

All selected functions are nonpayable and require zero native ETH. No direct KYC, caller role or pause modifier appears in these selected implementation bodies; available-balance/host/underlying checks still apply. Contract metadata does not establish interface availability or jurisdictional/legal eligibility, which remains the caller responsibility; the old console-linked superfluid.finance terms URL returned 404 and is not treated as permission to ignore terms.

functions.label: MDEX BSC Router addLiquidity
warnings: Caller selects token path/assets, amounts, recipient, deadline and financial minimums/maximums. Caller balances and token/LP allowances are required; metadata does not prove complete workflows or profitable/successful execution.

ETH-named native functions spend/return BNB on BSC through constructor-bound WBNB 0xbb4CdB9CBd36B01bD1cBaEBF2De08d9173bc095c. Payable calls can spend msg.value; nonpayable calls require zero native value.

The immutable factory supplies pair addresses, reserves and fee-aware quotes. Pairs are called with empty callback data; no caller-selected opaque executor or arbitrary callback is admitted. Factory fee configuration, pool liquidity and current runtime identity are not attested.

The owner can replace swapMining. Both swap loops may call that external hook before each pair swap; the returned bool is ignored, but a revert or incompatible hook can revert the transaction. Native account versus contract caller, restrict[pair], unrestricted[caller] and output/reserve thresholds condition reward-hook invocation; these are not swap-denial rules and no MDX reward is promised.

Fee-supporting swaps compute input from pair balance minus reserve. Token-output supporting swaps check recipient balance increase; supporting token-to-BNB swaps unwrap the entire router WBNB balance. Fee-supporting liquidity removal transfers the entire router token balance; burn-accounting minimums do not guarantee net post-tax receipts.

Liquidity-add minimum checks are branch-dependent: an empty pair uses both desired amounts without separate minimum checks; nonempty branches check only the calculated optimal-side amount. No minimum LP-token output exists. Deadlines, slippage/tax behavior and recipients remain caller responsibilities.

warnings: Calls target SatoshiXApp diamond, not raw facet. Exact StabilityPoolFacet source/ABI is selector-bound by facets() at BNB block 129288815. Diamond owner can replace selectors; static admission does not guarantee routing persists.

Deposit and withdrawal units are satUSD token base units (18 decimals), not dollars, collateral units or vault shares. provideToSP requires a positive amount and unpaused deposits. Exact debt token uses privileged sendToXApp transfer from caller, not transferFrom: this route does not consume ERC20 allowance.

Stability Pool deposits absorb liquidation debt and can decrease to zero; collateral gains accrue separately. Withdrawals are capped at the compounded remaining satUSD balance, not original deposit. Source rejects same-block deposit/withdraw using deposit timestamp < block.timestamp.

withdrawFromSP(0) updates accrual and snapshots but still requires an initial nonzero deposit and later timestamp. Deposits/withdrawals accrue collateral/rewards but do not pay collateral gains; claimCollateralGains is separate.

claimCollateralGains reads caller-owned gains and caller-selected stored collateral indexes; recipient is payout beneficiary, not an arbitrary execution target. Collateral token addresses come from configured storage. Out-of-range indexes, token failures or large index arrays can revert; use current index/token mapping. Amounts are each collateral token native base units.

Integer product/sum accounting, scale/epoch transitions, decimal normalization and floor rounding affect deposits and gains. No caller deadline, min-return guard or financial parameter validation is added.

Owner/role holders can pause deposits, sunset collateral, change reward distribution settings and upgrade diamond/token logic. Selected withdrawal source has no pause or pending-liquidation check; docs general withdrawal-pause statement is not silently substituted for exact deployed behavior.

Reward-token claim is excluded because current reward denomination/distribution dependency was not completely bound. Deposit/withdraw accrue rewards through configured community issuance; no reward availability or financial return claimed.
All selected functions are nonpayable. Exact selected source does not implement KYC or jurisdiction gates; website terms and independent authorization/pause policies remain authoritative.

Facet table is block-pinned research evidence; separate latest configuration reads are not atomic with it. Older-block config requests returned missing trie node. No fresh runtime identity, funding, liquidity, backing, execution or financial-safety guarantee is implied.

functions.label: Aster Claim caller processed USDF withdrawals
warnings: Static source/ABI inventory only; not proof of ongoing deployed identity, execution, funding, liquidity, backing, financial safety or a complete workflow. Exact grants, independent policies, pause checks and canonical calldata/value validation still apply. All selected methods require zero native value.

Aster is the single canonical product continuing Astherus/ApolloX, not three admissions. This target is own BNB Chain asUSDF Earn staking, not USDF issuer/admin minting, the Aster deposit bridge, derivatives account, aggregator, or third-party wrapper. Current docs identify this exact asUSDF minting contract and the BNB claim flow.

EIP1967 staking proxy currently binds implementation 0x29f30635431426363D130aa163816Ead1101662f; proxy source-service match is match, implementation exact_match. Immutable USDF 0x5a110fc00474038f6c02e89c707d638602ea44b5, asUSDF 0x917af46b3c3c6e1bb7286b9f59637fb7c65851fb and withdrawal vault 0xad4836bbf3671ebd4f2e1f49119c1184655e47ca match read-only responses. Vault currently binds 0x1A63fDbD396465A319b7Aea1dD9c0BF0A339BF89. Both proxies remain timelock-upgradeable, role-managed and independently pausable; identities are point-in-time, not persistent runtime attestations.

deposit pulls USDF from msg.sender into the staking proxy using allowance to that proxy; actual balance delta is used to floor-mint asUSDF to msg.sender at the pre-transfer exchange price. No arbitrary receiver, permit, opaque bytes or dynamic call target exists. Deposit requires positive amount, enabled deposits, unpaused staking and positive minted shares. Underlying/token role/transfer pauses can independently fail.

Exchange price is floor((USDF balance minus unvested rewards)*1e18/asUSDF total supply), with 1e18 fallback when supply or net balance is zero. Authorized reward distribution vests linearly over immutable 28800 seconds (8 hours); this is NOT a withdrawal waiting period. Prices and rounding can change; no user minimum shares/output, deadline or rate guarantee is present.

requestWithdraw fixes floor(asUSDF amount*current price/1e18) USDF payout, transfers that USDF to the fixed withdrawal vault, pulls caller asUSDF using allowance to the staking proxy, then burns it atomically. It records caller as receipt, current time/price and claimable=false. This is a caller-owned queue, not immediate redemption, and no cancellation method is exposed. Any later yield does not increase this fixed request payout.

claimWithdraw accepts request numbers but enforces recorded receipt == msg.sender, positive payout and claimable. It deletes the request and asks the fixed vault to transfer USDF only to msg.sender; batch failure reverts atomically, including duplicate/unavailable IDs. Claim needs staking and vault unpaused, withdrawals enabled, staking TRANSFER_ROLE at the vault and vault cash. These current role/cash conditions are not attested.

BOT_ROLE must explicitly mark withdrawal requests claimable; source has no automatic elapsed-time claim entitlement or hardcoded queue deadline. Docs describe T+1 hour (about 2 hours), but this is operational guidance, not guaranteed source-enforced timing. Requests can remain unclaimable if processing is delayed. Emergency withdrawal/whitelist operations are not admitted.

Selected staking source charges no mint/request/claim protocol fee and docs say asUSDF mint/withdraw no fees; gas is separate. USDF-to-USDT issuer redemption is a different product (documented fee/delay) and is not admitted. No yield, USDF backing/redemption or stable peg assurance is made.

USDF economic strategy relies on custodial/off-chain delta-neutral positions and funding fees, documented with Ceffu custody. Staking share accounting does not isolate this custody, strategy, centralized exchange, oracle or governance risk. No caller KYC/whitelist check appears on ordinary selected entrypoints, but app eligibility/jurisdiction and token restrictions remain.

functions.label: USDD buyGem caller-funded PSM conversion
warnings: Static deployment/source/ABI metadata only; not live authorization, persistent runtime attestation, liquidity, backing, yield, financial safety, successful execution or a complete workflow. Independent grants, policies, pauses and canonical calldata/value controls remain mandatory.

Current official Ethereum USDT/USDC and BNB Chain USDT PSM roots are directly deployed non-proxy UsddPsm/UsddPsm7 contracts; all three Sourcify runtime grades are match, not exact_match. Full matching original source and ABI plus point-in-time enabled-state observations are preserved. No Tron-only bridge, issuer mint role, Vat authorization, arbitrary executor or backend signature scope is admitted.

sellGem(usr,gemAmt) pulls caller collateral through its fixed authenticated GemJoin, opens/increases the PSM's own collateral/debt position, and sends resulting USDD to the specified financial recipient usr. buyGem(usr,gemAmt) pulls caller USDD using existing allowance, reduces PSM debt and returns the specified collateral amount to usr. Receiver choice does not grant spending authority over anyone else; no generic prefund/public-mint workaround or arbitrary calldata is used.

gemAmt is raw collateral units in both directions: Ethereum USDT and USDC use 6 decimals; BNB Chain USDT uses 18. USDD is 18-decimal wad. Conversion scales by 10^(18-gemDecimals). Exact-input swap outputs floor reserve formula; exact-output required inputs floor then add1. Library applies 99/100 input factor, a1% fee per hop, not ordinary Uniswap0.3%. Supply pulls only msg.sender underlying into the configured reserve aToken and mints onBehalfOf interest-bearing balances; first supply may enable collateral automatically. Withdrawal burns only msg.sender aToken balance and pays designated to (not the aToken); uint256 max means full current balance. Amounts are underlying token base units, not oracle currency or nominal property units. Supply/borrow caps, active/frozen/paused flags, reserve liquidity and health checks can prevent actions.

borrow releases underlying to msg.sender and mints debt for onBehalfOf; any applicable preexisting debt-token delegation/eligibility must already exist and is not granted here. Interest modes are 1 stable and 2 variable, subject to reserve enablement and stable-size restrictions. Debt accrues through reserve indexes/rates. Oracle, collateral LTV, liquidation threshold, health factor, isolation/silo/eMode rules and price-oracle sentinel constrain new loans; positions can be liquidated.

repay pulls only caller underlying and burns the selected debt account debt, capped at outstanding debt. uint256 max is allowed only when caller equals onBehalfOf; third-party debt repayment needs an explicit amount. repayWithATokens uses only caller aToken balance to repay caller debt; max uses caller balance and remains capped at debt. No permit, debt delegation or token approval is granted.

setUserUseReserveAsCollateral changes only caller financial collateral flags, requiring caller reserve balance and applicable isolation/LTV/health validation. setUserEMode changes only caller financial risk category with configured-category/debt-compatibility/health validation. These are own loan-risk state transitions, not wallet operator/role authorizations.

Pool supply/withdrawal/debt logic depends on mutable reserve aTokens/debt tokens, interest strategies, oracle and external linked code; issuer property-token transfer/KYC/whitelist controls may independently reject transfers. Neither product marketing nor catalog admission proves legal eligibility, property ownership, rental payments, backing, complete loan workflow or a payout schedule. Application feature flags/2FA UI are not a backend authorization grant; adapters/permit/flashloan/bridge/liquidation/admin paths are not admitted.

Native receiver payout uses empty calldata and can revert; all IDs in one redeem are atomic.

previewWithdraw/maxWithdraw getters do not establish a synchronous withdraw function or immediately available liquidity. warnings: Static exact-deployment source/ABI inventory only, not a fresh RPC/storage/runtime identity, successful-transaction or financial-safety guarantee. Grants, canonical calldata/value checks, balances, allowances, pauses and independent controls remain mandatory.

Monad mainnet chain143 gMON ERC1967Proxy 0x8498312A6B3CbD158bf0c93AbdCF29E6e4F55081; MonadScan currently reports MagmaV2 implementation 0xA1f511E1442c61931ca5ace7616d2cC78497aFd2. Initial deployment implementation 0x51f392f0D6232bF695B0C7F9bb145AA51c88d8BA is NOT the reviewed active interface. Owner can upgrade and change fees, redeem delay, MEV injector and pause state.

Native depositMON/depositMONGVault spend msg.value in native MON (18-decimal wei units), not ETH. deposit/depositWMON/depositWMONGVault and mint use WMON allowance to gMON; initial proxy deployment bound WMON 0x3bd359C1119dA7DA1D913d1C4D2B7c461115433A. Nonpayable calls require zero native value. Shares are 18-decimal gMON; no caller-set minShares/maxAssets, output minimum or deadline exists.

requestRedeem/requestRedeemGVault immediately burn nonzero shares and initiate asynchronous native staking undelegation. Caller must be share owner or an already approved operator; ERC20 share allowance alone is insufficient. Nonzero controller required; only one active request per owner. Capture returned/emitted requestId; requests do not continue earning vault yield. No cancellation entry is admitted or present.

redeem(uint256,address,address) is a claim by requestId, NOT standard ERC4626 share redemption. redeem pays WMON; redeemMON pays native MON. Stored claimableTime must be reached AND underlying Monad undelegation epochs/withdrawal IDs must be ready; frontend ~12-hour wait is not a guaranteed deadline. Controller, owner, either approved operator, or protocol owner may claim to the specified receiver.

Actual withdrawn MON minus current withdrawal fee is paid; slashing, validator cash and fees can reduce output. If withdrawal is below request.assets, implementation may mint residual gMON to receiver to socialize losses; it does not simply enforce a min(request-time,current-value) payout clamp despite its source comment. withdrawalFee/rewardsFee are mutable basis points up to10000 (100%). Native-output receiver must accept empty-calldata MON transfer.

gVault variants use explicit uint64 validator IDs and fixed delegate/undelegate methods, not arbitrary target/calldata. Validator whitelist/status/pause, relative/absolute caps, minimum deposit/withdrawal, existing per-validator ownership accounting and rebalances can restrict calls. gMON transferability does not transfer gVault per-user validator allocation; transferred shares may require pooled redemption instead.

CoreVault and gVault use mutable staking dependencies and cached delegation accounting. Cache refreshes and reward-claim guards occur inside ordinary calls; current pauses, minimums, caps, fees, stake capacity and runtime eligibility were not read. No KYC/access role gate appears on reviewed ordinary Magma entry points, but interface terms exclude US persons, sanctioned jurisdictions/persons and geographic bypass; permissionless ABI access is not legal eligibility.

Monad143 shMON proxy 0x1B68626dCa36c7fE922fD2d55E4f631d962dE19c currently points to explorer-reported ShMonad implementation 0x8Ee4FF5FF50198dcbB7B882A0781F42724Dd095f. Initial constructor implementation 0xbe59fC165fb8941d6d0De527e58Ff649a6fBe95c is not the reviewed interface. Code and governance can change; current storage/upgrade-authority configuration was not read.

deposit/mint use native MON, not WMON or an ERC20 allowance. MON assets and shMON shares use 18-decimal units. deposit requires msg.value exactly assets; mint requires msg.value exactly the execution-time ceil-rounded previewMint amount, so a prior quote may become stale. All other selected functions are nonpayable and require zero native value.

Only ordinary pooled uncommitted shMON is admitted. Commitments/policies, agents, top-ups, holds, delegated uncommit approvals, ERC20 approvals/transfers/permit, hMON zero-yield positions, isolated-validator stake, recovered principal, commissions and validator maintenance are excluded. Policy agents can spend committed funds and top up from uncommitted funds: no policy/agent authority is granted by ordinary staking admission.

Atomic withdraw/redeem burn owner uncommitted shares; caller other than owner needs existing share allowance. Native MON goes to explicit nonzero receiver, which must accept empty-calldata native transfer. Amounts are net MON for withdraw and shMON shares for redeem. Current liquidity, recent-revenue offsets, utilization fee and circuit breaker constrain execution.

Atomic fees follow mutable capped-linear utilization parameters, with a 1 gwei minimum when fees are enabled; that minimum can consume tiny outputs. Ordinary withdraw/redeem have no slippage bound. Protected variants atomically enforce maximum shares burned or minimum MON paid after the nested ordinary operation, reverting the entire transaction on failure. No selected method has a deadline.

requestUnstake burns caller nonzero uncommitted shares immediately and fixes a floor-rounded MON liability using recent-revenue-adjusted exchange rate; requests no longer earn rewards. Same completion epochs merge into up to seven pending buckets plus matured bucket. completionEpoch uses internal protocol epochs, normally native withdrawal delay plus four, with two additional epochs when global redemption capacity is insufficient.

completeUnstake pays every matured caller request directly to caller, leaving later requests queued. Completion requires internal epoch advancement/crank progress and sufficient redemption reserves or atomic-liquidity shortfall coverage; maturity is not a cash or wall-clock guarantee. No request ID, arbitrary receiver, operator approval or cancellation is accepted by these two pooled functions.

Closed mode blocks deposit/mint and traditional request/completion; atomic exits are not closed-gated but remain liquidity/circuit-breaker constrained. Frozen mode affects validator operations and may delay liquidity while ordinary pooled calls are not directly frozen-gated. Owner/governance can change fees, commissions, modes and implementations; documentation describes 3-day upgrade timelocks, not an independently read live timelock attestation.

Share conversion uses virtual +1 assets/shares with floor deposit/redeem and ceil mint/withdraw rounding; recent revenue is included on entry but excluded on exit, so immediate round trips can lose value. No role/KYC check appears on these ordinary implementation entries; source-level permissionlessness does not establish legal or frontend jurisdiction eligibility.

Underlying is six-decimal Monad USDC 0x754704Bc059F8C67012fEd69BC8A327a5aafb603; shares use underlying decimals (six here), not 18-decimal generic cToken units. Asset amounts in deposit/withdraw/borrow/repay are raw USDC atoms; mint/redeem/post/remove collateral use raw cUSDC shares. Deposits/mints/repayments require payer USDC allowance to this cToken.

Plain deposit/mint can fund any receiver without posting collateral. depositAsCollateral requires caller=receiver or an approved PositionManager; its For variant requires existing cToken delegate approval. postCollateral/removeCollateral operate on caller shares; For variants use existing delegate approval. No approval, permit or delegation-authority change is admitted.

withdraw/redeem and collateral-forcing variants burn owner shares and pay explicit receiver; non-owner calls need share allowance. redeemFor/redeemCollateralFor instead require existing delegate approval. Collateral variants force reduction of posted shares; plain exits may still remove collateral when required by balance accounting. Collateral/debt health, oracle checks and current market caps remain authoritative; posting collateral cannot be used while this account has debt in this same cToken, and borrowing cannot be used while it has collateral posted in this same cToken.

borrow attributes debt to caller and sends USDC to receiver; borrowFor needs existing owner delegate approval, not ERC20 allowance. repayFor can fund another owner without delegation. repay(0)/repayFor(0,owner) mean full accrued outstanding debt; positive excess repayment reverts. Partial repayment can fail minimum-loan-size/oracle review. Borrow/post-collateral resets account cooldown; current manager source enforces 20-minute minimum hold on repayments and collateral-reducing actions, not a guaranteed immediately executable exit.

Exits are synchronous only when enough actual USDC cash is held; otherwise they revert, with no redemption queue or claim capability. Interest accrual occurs before ordinary calls; accounting includes vested interest, outstanding debt and protocol interest fee rather than treating wallet cash as totalAssets. No caller-set minimum shares/output, maximum assets/rate or deadline exists. Deposit/redeem round down; mint/withdraw round up; zero-result financial amounts revert.

Constructor binds CentralRegistry 0x1310f352f1389969Ece6741671c4B919523912fF, MarketManager 0xa6A2A92F126b79Ee0804845ee6B52899b4491093 and initial IRM 0x1622D77E311638C77779e6D9B212E3e7D73AaFB4. IRM, protocol interest fee, market parameters, listing, pauses, delegation indexes and dependencies can change; constructor IRM is not asserted to be current. No separate deposit/withdraw transaction fee is coded in these ordinary cToken paths; protocol fees affect interest/yield. Protocol interestFee is capped at6000 basis points (60% of accrued interest). MarketManager consults CentralRegistry per-account transfer-disable controls on collateral-reducing paths; enabled ABI metadata cannot bypass them.

No KYC credential/allowlist gate appears in reviewed ordinary cToken methods; that is not legal eligibility. Interface terms exclude US-located/organized/resident and listed sanctioned/restricted jurisdictions/persons, require adult capacity and prohibit location-obscuring technology. No bridge, liquidation, flashloan, callback, arbitrary multicall, PositionManager action payload or administration capability admitted.

Path bytes are tokenA(20 bytes), custom deployer(20 bytes), tokenB(20 bytes), repeating deployer+token segments. Exact output reverses the path. Source does not enforce exact path length, and trailing bytes may be ignored; no custom payload/aggregator execution is admitted.

Pool/plugin fees, liquidity and token transfer behavior determine outcomes. The fee-on-transfer variant calls swapWithPaymentInAdvance and compares pool-reported output, not necessarily recipient net taxed-token receipts. A nonzero exact-output single price limit permits less than requested output; source requires full output only with limitSqrtPrice zero.

functions.label: Bean Exchange addLiquidity
warnings: Static exact-deployment source/ABI inventory only, not fresh RPC, storage, runtime identity, liquidity, successful execution or financial-safety attestation. Exact-function grants, canonical calldata/value checks, pauses, balances, allowances and independent controls remain mandatory.

Monad mainnet chain143 native currency is MON, not ETH. Constructor binds factory 0x8Bb9727Ca742C146563DccBAFb9308A234e1d242 and WMON 0x3bd359C1119dA7DA1D913d1C4D2B7c461115433A. Native input uses msg.value; nonpayable calls require zero native value. Token amounts use each token's raw decimals; bin liquidity amounts are per-bin LB share units.

Paths are explicit pairBinSteps and tokenPath arrays. Router obtains each pair from its immutable factory and invokes fixed swap(bool,address); no arbitrary target/calldata, permit, multicall or executor admitted. Factory-selected pair implementations and configurable hooks/fees are external dependencies, not caller-controlled executor payloads.

ERC20 inputs require allowance to this router. Removal burns msg.sender's per-bin positions and requires existing pair approveForAll(router,true), sufficient unlocked balances and matching ids/amounts. Authorization changes themselves are excluded. LP recipient and refundTo are independent; excess native liquidity is refunded as WMON by pair mint, not automatically native MON.

LiquidityParameters includes lockUntil: adding liquidity can lock the recipient's entire existing position in affected bins until a later timestamp. Locked shares cannot burn or transfer; source lock extension applies only when later than stored lock. Distribution entries are cast to uint64 before encoding and validated downstream; callers must choose coherent token ordering, bins, distributions, activeIdDesired/idSlippage, minimums, recipient and deadline. No minimum minted-LP-share argument exists.

Swaps enforce deadlines and min-output or max-input. Exact-output calculation narrows requested intermediate amounts to uint128; oversized inputs can truncate before downstream checks and are not automatically financially validated. Native exact-output refunds unused msg.value to caller, which must accept MON. Native recipients must accept empty-calldata transfers.

Fee-supporting exact-input swaps measure recipient output balance deltas (or router WMON delta for native output), not whole pre-existing router balance. Standard swap/minimum and liquidity removal checks use reported gross amounts and do not guarantee net fee-on-transfer receipts. removeLiquidityNATIVE explicitly does not support transfer-tax tokens. Dynamic swap/composition fees, integer rounding and factory-configurable pair hooks can affect output or revert calls.

Deployment source comes from Monad-documented BlockVision Sourcify service with exact creation/runtime matches; central Sourcify404 and MonadScan unverified do not replace this binding. Router is direct nonproxy; no current pool configuration or hook storage read is claimed. No caller KYC/role gate is present in reviewed ordinary router entries; interface/legal eligibility is not attested.

functions.label: OctoSwap add liquidity
warnings: Static deployment/source/ABI metadata only; no persistent runtime identity, funding, liquidity, execution, financial safety or complete-workflow assurance. Exact grants, independent policies, pauses and canonical calldata/value validation remain required.

Chain 143 is Monad mainnet. ETH-named payable parameters/functions mean native MON, not Ethereum ETH; WETH() is immutable WMON 0x3bd359c1119da7da1d913d1c4d2b7c461115433a. Only addLiquidityETH, swapExactETHForTokens and swapETHForExactTokens accept native value; every nonpayable selected function requires zero native value. addLiquidityETH and exact-output native swaps refund unused MON to msg.sender, whose recipient code must accept it.

This non-proxy Classic router binds immutable factory 0xce104732685b9d7b2f07a09d828f6b19786cda32 and pair init-code hash 0x1305842295bb388975eec146e164811bee4ac15606baa6205d5749e933f26762. Token path elements select factory-derived pairs, not arbitrary targets/selectors/bytes; router uses fixed pair.swap with empty callback bytes. Universal Router, multicall, CL router/position manager, permit, direct pair mint/burn, callbacks and admin capabilities are not admitted.

ERC20 input and both liquidity assets are pulled from msg.sender directly to the derived pair using prior router allowance; LP removal pulls caller LP shares to pair and burns them atomically. Recipient to is caller-selected and can differ from owner/caller. No delegated owner parameter or authorization is inferred. Never pre-fund pairs or router: pair mint/burn account for surplus balances and all LP shares already at the pair, so unrelated donations can alter results.

Swaps require a path of at least two tokens, active pairs and sufficient reserves. Native input paths start with WMON and native output paths end with WMON. Set intentional amountOutMin/amountInMax and deadline (Unix seconds, inclusive); all quantities use token base units. Exact-input outputs floor and exact-output inputs round up per hop; library applies 997/1000 input multiplier (0.3% pair fee). Fees, price movement and price impact remain economic risks, not guarantees.

Liquidity uses current reserve ratio and expiry. On addLiquidity, only the reduced/optimal side is checked against its minimum; the full desired side is not independently minimum-checked. Empty pools use both desired amounts directly without enforcing either minimum. There is no minimum-LP-share parameter. Initial pair mint permanently locks 1000 units; floor rounding and feeTo protocol LP minting affect shares/payout. removeLiquidity checks both gross pair-returned amounts, not net receipts after token taxes.

Only ordinary amount-preserving token paths/liquidity are selected. Rebasing, fee-on-transfer, denylisted, malicious or transfer-restricted assets can fail or give misleading output guarantees; supporting-fee variants that use router-wide balances and all permit variants remain excluded. Token contracts and native recipient callbacks are unavoidable configured/data-derived dependencies, not an isolation claim. No protocol KYC check appears in these router entrypoints, but app/jurisdiction/token restrictions and eligibility are not attested.

warnings: Static deployment/source/ABI metadata only; not live authorization, persistent runtime attestation, funding, backing, liquidity, financial safety, legal eligibility, successful execution or a complete workflow. Redeem claims floor assets, and withdraw computes floor shares while using ceil quantities to reduce entitlement; small residuals may be exhausted. Sourcify reports exact_match for this non-proxy deployment and retains immutable bindings/constructor evidence. functions.label: YO Protocol Deposit USDC for yoUSD
warnings: Static deployment/source inventory only, not fresh RPC/runtime/storage identity, liquidity, backing, financial safety or successful-execution assurance. Base yoUSD proxy uses explorer- and Sourcify-reported implementation 0xc84a6E01BFF58996540F1ABC22355A9DFE0d78DC. Upgrades, oracle pricing, fee recipient/rates, authority and pause state may change; current configuration is not attested.

Underlying is Base native USDC 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 with 6 decimals; yoUSD shares also use 6 decimals. deposit consumes exact gross USDC and mint requests exact yoUSD shares; caller needs USDC allowance to the vault. redeem and requestRedeem have identical instant-or-queued semantics: owner MUST equal msg.sender, shares > 0, receiver must be nonzero and not vault. If liquid USDC after pending reservations suffices, shares burn and USDC is sent; otherwise shares escrow and aggregate under receiver, return value 0. No separate user claim or user cancellation exists.

Queued redemptions require authorized fulfillment, which may be partial and can settle at request-time gross or a lower current-price value after exceptional losses. Live withdrawal fee applies when paid; original owner cannot cancel and privileged cancellation returns shares to receiver, not necessarily original owner. Documentation up-to-24-hour timing is not enforced or guaranteed.

Deposit/mint/exit have no caller min-shares/min-USDC/max-assets/deadline parameters. Oracle conversion and fee ceil/floor rounding apply; tiny positive deposit may produce zero shares. Fee calculations deduct configured fees even when recipient is zero, in which case fee funds stay in vault. Pause applies to deposits, redemptions and share movements. USDC restrictions can revert transfers; catalog does not grant legal eligibility or bypass underlying restrictions.

warnings: Static deployment/source inventory, not fresh RPC bytecode/storage/configuration or successful-execution proof. Active catalog status is not a live executability assertion. Base sKAITO is a direct StakedKAITO deployment, not a proxy. Underlying is 18-decimal KAITO 0x98d0baa52b2D063E780DE12F615f963Fe8537553; shares are 18-decimal sKAITO. Deposit/mint consume caller KAITO allowance to this exact vault; share amount is not raw KAITO amount. No permit or generic transfer authority is admitted.

Cooldown and synchronous exits are mutually exclusive modes. Constructor sets 7 days, but admin may set cooldownDuration anywhere from 0 to 90 days; no current duration is attested. With duration >0 use cooldownAssets/cooldownShares, which burn caller shares immediately and move KAITO to immutable AgingPool, then separately call claimFromAP(recipient) after maturity. With duration 0 only withdraw/redeem are enabled; any prior cooldown may be claimed immediately.

Cooldown requests aggregate per caller and each new request resets maturity for the ENTIRE accumulated lockedAmount. claimFromAP pays the full accumulated amount for msg.sender, not a user-selected owner or partial amount. No cancel request exists. Recipient must be a valid underlying-token recipient. Cooling funds no longer participate in vault share yield.

Blacklisting restricts caller/from/to share movement and withdrawal owner/recipient. Admin can redistribute blacklisted shares or burn them into vesting rewards; underlying rescue excludes KAITO. claimFromAP itself has no vault blacklist modifier, but must satisfy its own maturity and underlying transfer. Source does not require a deposit KYC allowlist; platform jurisdiction/sanctions/age restrictions and any separate launchpad KYC remain independent.

Nonzero assets and shares required; total share supply after deposit/exit must be either zero or at least 1e18 raw shares (global minimum, not a per-account minimum). Standard conversion has virtual +1 terms, rounds deposits/redeems down and mint/withdraw up. There is no caller minimum-output, maximum-input or deadline parameter. Remaining supply, rounding and share price can make small/full-balance actions revert.

Rewards are pushed by a restricted rewarder and linearly vest; constructor sets 7-day vesting and admin can change up to 90 days after current vest completes. No user reward-harvest call is admitted: claimFromAP claims an existing cooled principal amount, not separate staking rewards. No staking fee is charged in reviewed vault source; rates, funding, eligibility for off-chain incentives and financial results are not attested. Yaps retirement is not staking retirement; current official site still advertises native KAITO staking.

functions.label: Gamma Strategies Withdraw Base WETH-USDC vault liquidity
warnings: Static deployment-bound source/ABI inventory only, not a fresh runtime identity, current pool state, balance, liquidity, backing, successful execution or financial-safety guarantee. Exact grants, canonical calldata, pause overlays and independent controls remain mandatory; zero native value required.

Only current-app Base Aerodrome N WETH-USDC direct Hypervisor 0xa0f688905ef05ea853c35131b4899a613b4ba644 is admitted. Constructor binds pool 0xb2cc224c1c9fee385f8ad6a55b4d94e92359dc59 and reads immutable token0/token1 from it. Official current app maps token0 to 18-decimal Base WETH 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 and token1 to 6-decimal native USDC 0x833589fcd6edb6e08f4c7c32d4f71b54bda02913, not USDbC. Vault share decimals are 18; share amount is not a fixed raw token amount.

withdraw requires positive shares and nonzero recipient, then ultimately requires from == msg.sender and burns caller shares. Existing LP share allowance or approved operator does not authorize a different from. No LP approval is needed for the owner withdrawal. Outputs go to the explicit to recipient and remain WETH plus USDC, not native ETH.

Four minAmounts are base token0/token1 and limit token0/token1 liquidity burn minimums, not aggregate recipient output minimums. They are checked against amounts owed only for each nonzero liquidity position. Pro-rata unused balances are added afterwards. There is no deadline or aggregate min-output argument; floor rounding can reduce withdrawn position liquidity and dust outputs.

Before withdrawal, zeroBurn settles fees on both ranges, collects them to the vault and pays floor(owed/fee) to mutable feeRecipient. Source initial fee denominator is not asserted as current; owner can change fee without a range check. Zero fee can cause division-by-zero and block operations. Owner rebalancing/ranges, fee recipient, pool dependency and token behavior can affect or revert withdrawal. No onchain generic pause field exists in this exact interface.
