functions.label: Extra Finance Supply reserve underlying
warnings: Static source/ABI inventory only: no fresh runtime identity, funding, liquidity, execution success, complete workflow or financial-safety assurance. Exact-function grants, canonical calldata/value checks, pauses and independent controls still apply.

Current October 12, 2026 Aero-upgrade notice pauses ALL new borrowing on Base and OP from October 14; it asks legacy AERO/VELO suppliers to redeem for token upgrade, but explicitly says other lending suppliers do not need to migrate. This admission is the maintained lender interface, not leverage farming, new borrowing, or a revival of legacy AERO/VELO products. Check the chosen reserve and current upgrade notices; no new leverage is admitted.

reserveId chooses an owner-created active reserve, its underlying/eToken/staking contracts and token decimals; amount is underlying base units while redemption amounts are eToken base units, not fixed USD. Base constructor WETH9 is 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006. Current per-reserve active/frozen flags, assets, capacities and cash are not attested.

deposit atomically pulls underlying from msg.sender using allowance to LendingPool and mints eTokens to onBehalfOf. depositAndStake mints to LendingPool then approves and stakes in the reserve-configured staking contract for onBehalfOf; this does not claim rewards. Existing collateral/debt delegation is not an allowance substitute.

Payable deposits use native ETH for WETH reserves when the entire LendingPool native balance is at least amount; otherwise they pull ERC20. Send exact intended native amount for ETH funding and zero for ERC20 funding. With msg.value>0 refundETH sends the entire remaining native balance to caller. Forced/preexisting native balances can affect this branch; no standalone prefunding capability is admitted.

redeem transfers caller eTokens using eToken allowance to LendingPool; uint256.max means caller whole unstaked eToken balance. unStakeAndWithdraw instead withdraws exact positive eTokenAmount from caller staking balance through lending-pool-only settlement; it does NOT implement max-as-all and does not claim accrued rewards. Outputs go to explicit to, not a delegated owner.

All selected calls require global !paused and an active reserve. Deposits additionally reject frozen reserves and capacity overflow; redemptions require sufficient available underlying cash. No queue, delay guarantee, minimum shares/output or deadline. Exchange-rate calculations floor, potentially yielding zero shares/output. Reserve fee is interest accrued via treasury share minting: initial 15%, owner mutable up to 100%, not a current fixed fee or deposit charge.

receiveNativeETH unwraps only when underlying equals constructor WETH9; unwrap transfers the entire LendingPool WETH balance after burn, not merely the quoted output. Other assets remain ERC20 even if the bool is true. Treasury/address-registry, reserve token/staking dependencies, reward loops, linked libraries and owner changes can revert calls. Library source is compiler-input evidence, not independently verified current library identity.

Official July 23, 2025 Terms require legal age and lawful eligibility and prohibit US persons/residents, PRC, Cuba, North Korea, South Sudan, Iran, Syria and named sanctioned Ukraine regions, plus jurisdictions where prohibited. ABI access does not waive these restrictions; no KYC/legal-eligibility conclusion is made.

functions.label: QiDao Borrow MAI against cbBTC
warnings: Static source/ABI function inventory only; no current runtime identity, successful execution, funding, backing, liquidity, financial-safety or complete-workflow assurance. Calls require zero native value and remain subject to independent grants, pauses and canonical-calldata controls.

QiDao is the canonical brand for MAI Finance here, counted once. Current official site says MAI CDPs are fully live on Base and Polygon and legacy deployments are wound down. This admission is only the Base cbBTC vault, not any retired-chain migration/exit target.

Collateral is 8-decimal cbBTC 0xcbB7C0000aB88B473b1f5aFd9ef808440eed33Bf; debt is 18-decimal MAI 0xbf1aeA8670D2528E08334083616dD9C5F3B087aE. MAI and cbBTC base units are not interchangeable. cbBTC is an externally issued wrapped asset; no backing or custody assurance is made.

createVault mints the CDP ERC721 to caller. Borrow, collateral withdrawal and destroyVault require exact ownerOf(vaultID)==msg.sender, not merely an approved NFT operator. Borrowed MAI and withdrawn collateral go to caller; destroyVault returns remaining collateral to the recorded owner and requires zero debt.

depositCollateral and repayments accept an existing vault without requiring caller ownership, spend caller tokens via allowance and do not grant ownership. Their onlyRouter guard permits direct users only while router==address(0); the explorer rendering observed zero, but owner can change it. No router/executor capability is admitted.

borrow/repay require an existing registered front-end vault ID with promoter in (0,10000]. _front is a fee-accounting ID, not calldata/executor. Source fees are converted into collateral and deducted from the borrower CDP, then credited to the front-end CDP. Opening fee is calculated on new total debt, not just newly borrowed amount; the collateral-ratio check precedes deduction of that opening fee. Insufficient collateral for fees reverts.

Borrow requires positive amount, funded MAI in the vault, current debt limits and sufficient oracle-valued collateral. Interest accrues with time and is capitalized on debt updates; repayment must leave either zero debt or at least minDebt. paybackTokenAll takes a timestamp deadline and transfers current accrued MAI debt; other selected CDP calls have no caller deadline/min-output/fee/rate guard.

Explorer rendering observed minimum collateral percentage=125, annual iR=1000 basis points, openingFee=closingFee=0, minDebt=10e18 and maxDebt=500000e18. These owner-mutable point-in-time values are not lasting financial terms or guaranteed available borrowing. Oracles, front-end configuration and debt parameters can change or cause reverts.

getPaid claims already-recorded maticDebt entitlement in cbBTC despite its MATIC-based variable name; getPaid(address) can be triggered by anyone but pays only that entitled address, never a caller-chosen redirection of another account’s claim. It requires nonzero entitlement. This does not admit liquidation, distressed-vault acquisition or operator interest extraction.

No asynchronous withdrawal queue or fixed repayment delay is implemented in these reviewed CDP methods. Transfers depend on token behavior and available contract assets. Source owner/router/front-end gates remain authoritative. No explicit KYC/jurisdiction allowlist is in these ordinary vault functions; contract availability is not legal eligibility or custody/funding assurance.

QiDao is the canonical brand for MAI Finance here, counted once. Current official site says MAI CDPs are fully live on Base and Polygon and legacy deployments are wound down. This admission is only the Base cbBTC vault, not any retired-chain migration/exit target.

Collateral is 8-decimal cbBTC 0xcbB7C0000aB88B473b1f5aFd9ef808440eed33Bf; debt is 18-decimal MAI 0xbf1aeA8670D2528E08334083616dD9C5F3B087aE. MAI and cbBTC base units are not interchangeable. cbBTC is an externally issued wrapped asset; no backing or custody assurance is made.

createVault mints the CDP ERC721 to caller. Borrow, collateral withdrawal and destroyVault require exact ownerOf(vaultID)==msg.sender, not merely an approved NFT operator. Borrowed MAI and withdrawn collateral go to caller; destroyVault returns remaining collateral to the recorded owner and requires zero debt.

depositCollateral and repayments accept an existing vault without requiring caller ownership, spend caller tokens via allowance and do not grant ownership. Their onlyRouter guard permits direct users only while router==address(0); the explorer rendering observed zero, but owner can change it. No router/executor capability is admitted.

borrow/repay require an existing registered front-end vault ID with promoter in (0,10000]. _front is a fee-accounting ID, not calldata/executor. Source fees are converted into collateral and deducted from the borrower CDP, then credited to the front-end CDP. Opening fee is calculated on new total debt, not just newly borrowed amount; the collateral-ratio check precedes deduction of that opening fee. Insufficient collateral for fees reverts.

Borrow requires positive amount, funded MAI in the vault, current debt limits and sufficient oracle-valued collateral. Interest accrues with time and is capitalized on debt updates; repayment must leave either zero debt or at least minDebt. paybackTokenAll takes a timestamp deadline and transfers current accrued MAI debt; other selected CDP calls have no caller deadline/min-output/fee/rate guard.

Explorer rendering observed minimum collateral percentage=125, annual iR=1000 basis points, openingFee=closingFee=0, minDebt=10e18 and maxDebt=500000e18. These owner-mutable point-in-time values are not lasting financial terms or guaranteed available borrowing. Oracles, front-end configuration and debt parameters can change or cause reverts.

getPaid claims already-recorded maticDebt entitlement in cbBTC despite its MATIC-based variable name; getPaid(address) can be triggered by anyone but pays only that entitled address, never a caller-chosen redirection of another account’s claim. It requires nonzero entitlement. This does not admit liquidation, distressed-vault acquisition or operator interest extraction.

No asynchronous withdrawal queue or fixed repayment delay is implemented in these reviewed CDP methods. Transfers depend on token behavior and available contract assets. Source owner/router/front-end gates remain authoritative. No explicit KYC/jurisdiction allowlist is in these ordinary vault functions; contract availability is not legal eligibility or custody/funding assurance.

functions.label: Aera Request own USDC deposit into gtUSDa
warnings: Static deployment/source/ABI metadata only, not live authorization, persistent runtime attestation, liquidity, backing, safety, successful execution or a complete workflow. Catalog inclusion grants no permissions or eligibility; independent grants, policies, pauses and canonical calldata/value validation remain mandatory. All selected methods are nonpayable and require zero native value.

Exact current Base gtUSDa MultiDepositorVault 0x000000000001CdB57E58Fa75Fe420a0f4D6640D5 routes to non-proxy ProvisionerV2 0x128Afda4351deCE9d51Eb9d7e9C687C58cfff731 and non-proxy PriceAndFeeCalculatorV2 0xa90fd5C2020DBf19c6c29609dF85F7e4DBAC30db. Current getters supersede the older provisioner/calculator still listed in the Gauntlet deployment table. Aera official documentation explicitly requires discovering these mutable dependencies; catalog addresses do not auto-follow rotations.

At Base block 52994616, vault and calculator vault-paused reads are false; USDC token configuration enables async deposit/redeem and disables sync deposit/redeem; async multipliers are 10000/10000. Cancellation toggles are false. These are point-in-time configuration observations, not future availability promises.

The admitted seven-argument requestDeposit and requestRedeem wrappers fix receiver=msg.sender. Deposit pulls caller USDC to the provisioner; redeem pulls caller gtUSDa shares to escrow. Separate preexisting ERC20 allowances are required and not granted here. USDC uses 6 decimals; vault units use 18. No standalone prefunding/mint shortcut or third-party share authority is admitted.

Requests escrow funds until solver settlement or expiry refund. They require positive input and minimum output, a future deadline no more than 365 days away, an enabled token and an unpaused calculator. Automatic requests use the active price at solving, user maxPriceAge, configured token multiplier and floor rounding; solverTip is denominated in underlying tokens and reduces effective input/output. Fixed-price requests require zero explicit tip and may deliver only the requested minimum while a direct solver retains the difference.

Aera flagship integration instructions say use Base USDC 0x833589fcd6edb6e08f4c7c32d4f71b54bda02913, solverTip=0, and finite deadlines; ordinary solver fill time is not guaranteed. Do not copy a stale quote or treat suggested slippage buffers as financial advice. Source permits configured tokens beyond USDC, but only current enabled-token state is evidence; token restrictions and fee-on-transfer/rebasing behavior may break nominal-flow assumptions.

refundRequest(address,(uint8,address,address,uint256,uint256,uint256,uint256,uint256)) uses the full original RequestV2 (type,user,receiver,units,tokens,tip,deadline,maxPriceAge) to find and clear an existing escrow hash. Anyone may call after deadline strictly precedes block.timestamp; early refund requires preexisting authorization. Refund goes to the recorded receiver with recorded requester fallback if receiver transfer fails. Admitted own-request wrappers set both to the caller; the typed tuple does not contain executable strategy bytes or create permissions.

Vault guardian submit, solveRequestsVault with opaque bytes, solver settlement, callbacks, role/ownership/authority changes, depositReceiverApproval, and approvals/transfers are excluded. Synchronous deposit/mint/redeem/withdraw and early cancellation are excluded because current USDC configuration disables them. Vault whitelist, mutable transfer hook, calculator prices/fees, guardian-managed positions and settlement liquidity may restrict ordinary entry/exit; no guardian execution or complete dependency/security review is asserted.

This is SSI own managed multi-chain index issuance, not CEX holdings or a curator label. Only existing KYB-approved Whitelisted Participants can request mint/redeem for an assetID; catalog inclusion never enrolls a caller, grants issuer roles, obtains a maker quote or establishes legal/jurisdictional eligibility.

addMintRequest requires order.requester=msg.sender, membership, configured min/max index amounts and issue fee <= maxIssueFee, collected token fees, no rebalancing and a valid maker-signed order. It pulls each local-chain input ERC20 from the caller into the issuer, including the issue fee, records a PENDING request and locks index issuance. It does NOT mint immediately. Fixed swap validation/financial calls carry typed order data, not arbitrary target/selector/calldata execution.

addRedeemRequest requires the same eligibility and request gates plus current issuer role on the index token. It pulls caller-owned index shares into escrow; the input basket must exactly match the current index basket. Every output token must be local-chain and output destination must be this issuer. It records the pending request and locks issuance; no immediate burn or payout occurs.

Quote orderSign is a preexisting authorized MAKER signature, not a new wallet signing capability. Current Swap checks order hash, deadline, replay, maker role/signature, chain, allowlisted token identities and output addresses. Ordinary requests depend on mutable factory-selected token/swap contracts and owner/maker settlement. Underlying portfolio custody may span other chains; no bridge, other-chain target, maker execution, arbitrary trade/rebalance or authorization function is admitted.

Owner confirmMintRequest later finalizes swap transfers and mints only to the recorded requester. Owner confirmRedeemRequest later burns escrow and either pays net local-chain output directly to requester or credits claimables when force=true. Owner rejection can refund mint inputs directly or credit claims; redemption rejection returns escrow shares. These owner/maker functions are excluded. No settlement deadline, available liquidity, cancellation or guaranteed recovery is promised; source cancellation implementations are commented out and absent from ABI.

claim(token) pays only claimables[token][msg.sender], zeroes that credit and reduces aggregate reserved claims before sending the selected ERC20 to msg.sender. It cannot choose another owner or receiver, and is available only after owner-recorded claim credit. It is also whenNotPaused; a pending request is not itself a claimable amount.

Index amounts use 8 decimals. Input/output basket token quantities are floor(token.amount * order.inAmount/outAmount / 1e8) in each token base unit; issue fee floors token quantity * issueFee / 1e8, added at mint and subtracted at redeem. maxIssueFee caps the configured issue fee only, not custody spread, management fees, quote suitability or execution slippage. Order quantities/deadline are maker-quoted; there is no separate user min-output argument.

MAG7 issue fee reads zero and a nonempty preexisting participant list exists. Mutable point-in-time settings do not guarantee any caller eligibility or future enabled state.

Factory, swap and MAG7 are upgradeable dependencies; their current implementations and full matching implementation sources are retained. Factory owner may change issuers, swaps, fee managers, vault and token implementation subject to source gates. Selected ABI accepts assetID generally, but only the exact own SSI product resolved through current factory state is intended; no broad market coverage, backing or portfolio custody assurance is asserted. burnFor only destroys caller shares without proceeds and is excluded.

functions.label: iAero Protocol claim iAERO staking/rewards
warnings: Static source/ABI deployment metadata only; not live authorization, persistent runtime attestation, backing, liquidity, financial safety, yield, successful execution or a complete workflow. Independent grants, policies, pauses and canonical calldata/value controls remain mandatory; zero native value required.

Only the maintained Base EpochStakingDistributor is admitted. The 22 October 2026 primary migration notice explicitly says iAERO staking, unstaking and reward claiming work normally. Retired PermalockVault V5 AERO/veNFT deposits are paused and excluded; the future sAERO vault is not admitted. Staking is iAERO receipt staking, not a redeemable AERO lock or another Aerodrome label.

stake and stakeFor pull iAERO only from msg.sender; stakeFor credits the specified nonzero beneficiary. Amounts are iAERO base units (18 decimals); ledger and optional stiAERO mint are 1:1 without a minimum-output or deadline argument. The code credits the requested amount, not a transfer balance delta.

unstake and exit reduce only the caller staking ledger, burn caller stiAERO if the receipt is configured, and return iAERO to the caller. Transferable receipts do not transfer the staking ledger; a caller who moved receipts away may be unable to unstake until holding enough to burn. exit withdraws principal only and does not claim rewards.

Rewards use seven-day epoch-start snapshots and floor(total funded * caller balance / total supply), less already claimed. New mid-epoch stakes need not earn that epoch. Zero-supply epochs can leave funded rewards unclaimable. claimMany requires equal arrays and at most 50 entries; claimLatest visits current and previous epochs with no source-enforced token-list cap.

Reward token addresses select fixed ERC20/native payout accounting, not arbitrary executable calldata. address(0) denotes ETH rewards; all selected methods are nonpayable. Rewards go only to msg.sender; no payout or reward existence is promised.

Owner can pause staking, exits and claims, alter the receipt pointer until frozen, authorize reward funders and recover non-iAERO/non-receipt reward tokens, potentially removing reward backing. Receipt mint/burn role linkage is a dependency, not a permission granted here. No live receipt pointer, freeze or pause claim is made.

functions.label: Pinto deposit Silo deposit/accounting and own claims
warnings: Static deployment/source/ABI metadata only; not live authorization, persistent runtime attestation, liquidity, backing, yield, financial safety, successful execution or a complete workflow. Independent grants, policies, pauses and canonical calldata/value controls remain mandatory.

Base Pinto Protocol diamond only. Current loupe returned 32 facets and 354 routed function selectors, preserved in evidence. SiloFacet 0x051b60dad9c5a87355ffc5fb795c00e95c849a2a and ClaimFacet 0xab86a40c4aeb2af5e739bfdb66f21fd4ca9e7098 have Sourcify runtime match, not exact_match. Diamond upgrades, whitelist, PDV functions and dependencies remain mutable; paused() was false at observation, not a continuing availability guarantee.

Direct calls use LibTractor._user(), which falls back to msg.sender outside an active Tractor context. No Tractor, farm, pipeline, token/deposit transfers, approvals, permits or backend typed-data signing are admitted. Mow variants can update a named account's accrued Stalk but cannot redirect its assets or claim its rewards; no delegated authority is granted.

Deposit amounts are raw native token units: PINTO has 6 decimals, LP tokens use their own decimals; do not substitute PDV or Stalk units. PDV/BDV is Pinto-denominated accounting, not a USD redemption promise. stem is a signed int96 accrual index identifying a deposit, not a timestamp or token quantity. Stalk rewards use integer arithmetic and configured per-PDV factors.

From mode 0 EXTERNAL pulls caller tokens by existing ERC20 allowance; 1 INTERNAL debits own internal ledger exactly; 2 EXTERNAL_INTERNAL uses internal first then pulls shortfall; 3 INTERNAL_TOLERANT uses only available own internal balance and can fund less than requested. Actual external receipts are measured by token balance delta. Deposit credits actual received amount and configured PDV; positive PDV and current token whitelist are required. No raw shared-pool prefund/public-mint path is used.

To mode 0 EXTERNAL sends withdrawal/claim to caller wallet; 1 INTERNAL credits caller ledger while tokens remain in diamond custody. Withdrawal consumes own token/stem deposit amount and burns its associated base/grown Stalk and roots or germinating Stalk. Partial deposit removal rounds removed PDV up using ceil(amount*cratePDV/crateAmount); batch stems/amounts must match. No protocol withdrawal queue or mandatory withdrawal lock appears in these selected bodies; custody and token transfer can still fail.

New deposits germinate for one full Season before earning new Pinto mints; nominal Season is 3600 seconds, not guaranteed wall-clock settlement. Germination is reward eligibility, not an exit lock. Withdrawals forfeit the corresponding Stalk/Seeds earning position, and LP exits here return LP tokens, not their underlying assets. No separate explicit fee is charged by these selected Silo bodies; token behavior, gas, PDV rounding and economic losses remain material.

plant() claims only accrued caller Earned Pinto into a Silo deposit, not wallet cash; earned-Pinto calculation floors roots/stalk pro-rata conversion and caps to system earned balance. Planted earnings bypass germination. Mow only realizes accrued Stalk accounting without external token payout. claimPlenty/claimAllPlenty return already-recorded caller Flood rewards in each eligible Well's non-Pinto token, in that token's native units, clearing the recorded entitlement; they do not execute a user-supplied swap or promise future rewards.

These functions are payable for protocol composition but ordinary direct Silo/accounting calls need no native ETH: send zero native value; selected bodies provide no native-ETH refund guarantee. Only source-bound direct methods are cataloged. Runtime identities, mutable token hooks, oracle/pool behavior, financial solvency and downstream dependency safety are not independently attested.

Owner can change parameters, freeze/emergency state and assimilators; factory global freeze, pool caps and guarded per-user balance limits may reject deposits/swaps.

Finite pool asset/receiver handling only: registered origin/target assets choose configured assimilators, not arbitrary calls; swaps pay msg.sender, deposits mint LP to msg.sender, withdrawals burn only caller LP and pay caller. No transfer/approval/admin/flash callback/executor capability is granted.

Liquidity deposit is an 18-decimal numeraire value, NOT an amount of either EURC or USDC; actual two-token funding uses pool ratios and raw native token units. Base/quote minima/maxima apply through the existing-liquidity assimilator branch, not the empty-pool branch. LP amounts use 18 decimals. Fixed-point conversion adds ONE_WEI on deposits and floors raw conversion; do not assume exact value or zero loss.

Swap input/output and their maxima/minima use native token units. Exact-input originSwap enforces minimum target output, exact-output targetSwap enforces maximum origin funding. Actual deadline guard is block.timestamp < deadline (Unix seconds), despite stale source comments saying block number. Dynamic curve fees plus epsilon and factory treasury split affect settlement.

withdraw returns proportional underlying basket using oracle/assimilator conversions, not a 1:1 claim or single asset; it has no per-token minimum output parameter, and no queue in this reviewed surface. LPs face FX, depeg, oracle, pool-imbalance, rounding and loss risk. Emergency-only withdrawal is inventoried but not activated.

Configured assimilators are delegated fixed financial interfaces and custody/funding dependencies. Constructor EURC assimilator 0x97f8bf444bfc3052ae60a8ca50a0257daa440295 and USDC assimilator 0x53b105e1d48a76cdb955d037f042c830d14d82ab pull only msg.sender funding in preserved source. Full dependency runtime/current configuration, linked-library safety, issuer reserve backing and financial safety are not attested; mutable replacements can change behavior.

Mint pulls only caller collateral to the configured lending manager and mints jEUR to the fixed financial recipient field. Redeem pulls and burns only caller synthetic tokens, withdrawing collateral to recipient. Approval balances are external prerequisites; token approvals, permits, backend typed-data signing, registration, roles, lending-manager rewards and migrations are not admitted.

Collateral and all collateral minima/fees/liquidity amounts use native USDC units (6 decimals); synthetic quantities/minima are 18-decimal jEUR units. Oracle prices, fees and LP overcollateralization ratios use 18-decimal fixed point, not integer percentages. Mint deducts fee before price conversion; redeem deducts fee from gross collateral. Division/conversion round down and lending-token dust can alter actual credited/debited/received amounts.

functions.label: DackieSwap addLiquidity caller-funded V2 liquidity/swap
warnings: Static deployment/source/ABI metadata only; not live authorization, persistent runtime attestation, liquidity, backing, financial safety, successful execution or a complete workflow. Independent grants, policies, pauses and canonical calldata/value controls remain mandatory.

Base DackieV2Router only: nonproxy DackieRouter with immutable factory and WETH, deployed verified exact-match source. V2 liquidity is still documented as a current own-product surface; newer Meta Aggregator positioning is not evidence of V2 retirement. No SmartRouter, aggregator executor, V3, farms, permit or signing scope is added.

All selected methods pull msg.sender tokens or LP shares, or consume supplied native ETH; outputs go to caller-specified to. Token and LP allowances must already exist; this catalog grants no approvals. Amounts use each asset native units, LP liquidity uses pair LP units; deadlines use block.timestamp seconds. Native ETH uses18 decimals.

Paths are token sequences routed only through deterministic factory pairs; pair swap callback bytes are always empty. No arbitrary target/calldata executor. Mutable token behavior and independently unreviewed pair dependencies remain outside runtime attestation.

Exact-input swaps enforce minimum output; exact-output swaps enforce maximum input and round required input up. DackieLibrary calculates swap fee using9975/10000 (0.25%), not the generic docs example0.3%. LP additions optimize reserve ratios and can create a missing pair; initial empty-pair branch takes desired amounts directly. There is no return/yield or loss guarantee.

ETH-input liquidity/exact-output swaps refund unused native ETH to msg.sender. ETH-output methods unwrap WETH and pay to; transfer failure reverts. Fee-on-transfer swaps measure receiver balance delta for token output, but ETH output uses router total WETH balance; fee-on-transfer LP removal checks gross amounts then sends router total token balance, so token receiver net minimum is not guaranteed. Nonpayable calls require zero native value.

functions.label: Surge Credit deposit own variable USDC share ledger
warnings: Static deployment/source/ABI metadata only; not live authorization, persistent runtime attestation, liquidity, backing, financial safety, successful execution or a complete workflow. Independent grants, policies, pauses and canonical calldata/value controls remain mandatory.

Base variable earn market0 only, USDC6-decimal asset per primary docs. Root ERC1967Proxy0xee755f1bbcbf6e3260469d0f473522d71d3bddda is explorer similar-match source (not relabeled exact); explorer current implementation0xf289be5befea870689a9769db0738419ba8f1a79 is LiquidityPoolV3 verified exact match. Current implementation resolution is explorer-reported; public Base RPC storage reads were403. Owner UUPS upgrades and provider/admin dependencies remain mutable.

Deposits pull configured market0 token only from msg.sender and credit nontransferable internal supplyShares to msg.sender. Market must exist and be active; deposit is whenNotPaused, but no live paused state is asserted. USDC allowance must already exist; no authorization/grant methods are added.

All selected calls accrue interest through configured provider first. First deposit uses1:1 shares; subsequent deposits floor amount*1e18/supplyExchangeRate and have no minimum-share or deadline argument. Withdraw(amount) uses asset units (not shares), burns shares rounded up, checks own claim and physical idle liquidity, then transfers only to msg.sender.

withdrawAll accepts only marketId0, burns all caller market0 shares, pays floor(shares*exchangeRate/1e18), and requires enough liquidity for the whole claim; it is not a partial max-withdraw helper. Neither withdraw method has whenNotPaused in this implementation. Withdrawals remove depositor-queue membership only when no remaining positions/locked allocations exist.

These are variable-share ledger operations, not generic ERC4626. Fixed-market exposure selection, fixed allocation/exit queues and administrative replacement-LP settlement are excluded from this variable-only scope. Existing fixed allocations cannot be exited through withdraw/withdrawAll.

Lenders bear losses: liquidation settlement can reduce supply assets/exchange rate; rate floor1 prevents division-by-zero after total loss but does not preserve principal. Protocol reserve cut mints protocol shares. Source includes linked PoolLogicLib delegatecall and configurable rate provider; independent dependency runtime attestation is not established. All selected functions require zero native value.

functions.label: Kokonut Swap addLiquidity caller-funded Base router
warnings: Static deployment/source/ABI inventory only; not live authorization, persistent runtime attestation, balances, liquidity, financial safety, successful execution or complete workflow. Independent grants, pauses and canonical calldata/native-value controls remain mandatory.

Base8453 own Kokonut Router0x9d6328733daa5b4c7fee596ec7e73a935d799179 is selected by current official Base frontend mainnet configuration. Full Sourcify root source has exact_match creation/runtime and proxyResolution.isProxy=false; no proxy implementation substituted. The frontend-linked old repository404 is a source-link gap, not a shutdown claim; complete deployed source is retained independently.

Fixed financial interfaces only: caller supplies pool/token path and integer swap parameters, not executable bytes or an arbitrary-call target/value/calldata bundle. Router calls only typed pool/token/WETH methods, with empty callback data for exchanges. It checks pool coin indices match input/output. No signing, approval capability, bridge, admin or generic executor is admitted; internal approvals to chosen pools persist at uint256 max and create pool-dependency exposure.

swapWithPath pulls amount of the first ERC20 from msg.sender or wraps native ETH for a zero-address input. For native input, excess msg.value over amount is refunded; if msg.value is less than amount, missing input is pulled from caller as WETH. Non-native input requires msg.value=0. A zero-address output unwraps WETH and transfers ETH to msg.sender; token output also goes only to msg.sender.

Path is [token,pool,token,...] with swapParams entries [inputIndex,outputIndex,poolType], poolType1 stable exchange,2 meta underlying exchange,3 crypto exchange. Intermediate swap minima are0; only final minAmount constrains receipt. No deadline, output receiver, max-hop guarantee or per-hop slippage bound is provided. Despite source comments mentioning4 rounds, loop bound follows path.length, not a hard4-hop limit.

Router uses its entire current balance of each output token as subsequent input and final payout, rather than a per-call balance delta; do not pre-fund router or assume stranded balances belong to caller. Pool return dy is recorded in outputs but actual balance drives subsequent hops/payout; returned per-hop outputs can differ from final payout for nonstandard tokens. Token-native decimals apply; pool fees/rounding and fee-on-transfer behavior remain dependency-specific.

addLiquidity asks pool N_COINS and coins(i), requires matching amounts length, pulls caller amounts, adds msg.value to each WETH coin amount and wraps it, then invokes one of fixed poolType1/2/3 addLiquidity with minMintAmount; resulting LP token reported by pool is sent to msg.sender. No ownership/delegation, arbitrary payload or public prefunding mint workaround. ETH should be zero unless the selected pool contains the expected WETH coin; the router does not explicitly refund ETH on pools without WETH.

User-selected pools and token contracts remain external dependencies, not independently runtime-attested by this catalog entry. Current factory/pool changes, pool pause state, pricing/fees, approvals, transfer behavior, solvency and capacity can affect outcomes. No supplied path/pool or live pool availability is endorsed; catalog admits only this fixed router interface.

functions.label: MUX Cancel owned pending order
warnings: Static deployment-bound ABI/source inventory, not fresh runtime bytecode/storage identity, balances, allowance, liquidity, financial-safety or successful-execution assurance. Exact grants, canonical calldata/value validation, pauses and independent controls remain mandatory.

Arbitrum MUX V1 MUXLP OrderBook proxy is 0xa19fD5aB6C8DCffa2A295F78a5Bb4aC543AAF5e3. Current Sourcify proxyResolution reports 0xaB66dfEf3722Db73930A59147d900544D7B2AE90, differing from old official docs 0xFD92e0b7107488b095cA98E50BE128fee2a35879. Only actual current implementation ABI/source is used; service labels its implementation match/match, not exact_match. Linked LibOrderBook is 0x09a0dbd7667236106322f6254b605d51e36d4b6b and its bound source matches.

placeLiquidityOrder(uint8,uint96,bool) creates escrowed delayed order, not immediate LP mint or withdrawal. assetId is protocol pool asset index, not arbitrary call target. isAdding=true spends raw asset units and buys 18-decimal MUXLP; false escrows raw 18-decimal MUXLP and selects output asset. Inputs transfer atomically from caller; no separate prefund step.

For adds whose pool asset equals configured WETH, exact native ETH value rawAmount is required and wrapped internally; supplying WETH with zero value does not substitute. Other ERC20 adds require zero value and allowance to OrderBook. MUXLP sells require MUXLP allowance and should send zero value; the sell branch does not reject stray ETH and can strand it. rawAmount=0 is only a whitelisted-callback-account mode, not an ordinary zero-amount order.

Only brokers fill orders after mutable liquidityLockPeriod. Current docs say 18 minutes; older tutorial says around 15 minutes. Neither is asserted as current storage. Owner may set lock up to 30 days; cancellation requires order owner and mutable cancelCoolDown. No caller-set min output, price bound or deadline exists for liquidity orders, and no guaranteed fill time/automatic settlement is supplied.

cancelOrder(uint64) cancels caller-owned pending liquidity orders after cooldown, returns escrowed input (native ETH via configured unwrapper for WETH-backed adds; MUXLP for sells). This ABI also cancels owned position/withdrawal/rebalance orders under source-specific authority/expiry checks, and brokers can cancel expired position/withdrawal orders. It does not authorize creating those excluded leveraged workflows.

Filled outputs go to stored order account. Configured pool/oracle/broker prices, base plus dynamic imbalance fees, bid/ask spreads, 18-decimal normalization, flooring and liquid reserves determine result. No fixed fee rate or price is asserted. Pool requires enabled/listed liquidity asset and MLP-price bounds; insufficient reserves and dependency failures can prevent fills. liquidity-order pause gates fill, not placement or owner cancellation in this reviewed OrderBook.

Owner-configured callbackWhitelist causes fixed ILiquidityCallback calls on the order account before/after fill and after cancel, with configured gas limit; before-fill false/revert cancels, after-fill can revert, after-cancel failure is ignored. No arbitrary target or payload is supplied by these admitted parameters. No callbacks, callback administration, broker fills, rebalance, generic multicall, V3 prefunding helper or leveraged router is admitted.

Current official docs continue to describe V1 MUXLP buys/sells alongside V3. May 2026 wind-down forum topic is a community proposal, not an adopted shutdown notice; contributor Jean explicitly says protocol continues in maintenance mode with bugs addressed regularly. This is not a TVL/activity/performance assertion or guarantee of team continuity. No contract KYC gate appears for selected ordinary V1 calls; user jurisdiction eligibility remains independent.

functions.label: Nerite Add WETH collateral
warnings: Static deployment-bound source/ABI inventory only; no current bytecode/storage identity, execution, liquidity, collateral backing or financial-safety guarantee. Exact grants, canonical calldata, pauses and independent controls remain mandatory. All selected calls require zero native value.

Targets only the direct Arbitrum WETH BorrowerOperations branch, not another collateral, zapper, leverage executor, USND streaming, bridge or Liquity Ethereum deployment. Source keeps Bold names but debt token is official USND 0x4ecf61a6c2fab8a047ceb3b3b263b401763e9d49. Collateral is 18-decimal WETH 0x82af49447d8a07e3bd95bd0d56f35241523fbab1; native ETH is not accepted.

Opening pulls WETH collateral plus 0.001 WETH gas reserve from caller using existing BorrowerOperations allowance, mints USND to caller, and gives the position NFT to specified owner; trove ID hashes caller, owner and ownerIndex. Owner/addManager/removeManager/receiver fields are authority-sensitive, not arbitrary call targets: source stores managers and a remove-manager receiver. This catalog does not set or constrain them automatically or grant those roles. Separate manager-setting and batch-registration methods are excluded.

Increasing collateral or repaying debt requires NFT owner or allowed add/remove manager; zero addManager allows anyone to contribute. Withdrawing collateral, borrowing and closing require owner or remove manager. Outputs go to NFT owner unless an authorized remove manager has configured a receiver. NFT-approved operators alone are not accepted by these checks. Close burns caller entire USND debt and returns collateral plus gas reserve to the authorized receiver; no USND approval is needed for protocol burn.

Minimum debt is 500 USND (500e18), not Liquity 2000 BOLD. Annual rate is 1e18-scaled and source range is 0.5% through 250%. Debt increases accrue upfront fee based on branch approximate average interest and seven-day period, bounded by caller maxUpfrontFee. Rate adjustment within seven days can charge upfront fee; delegated rate authority and its bounds remain enforced. No assumed current rate or batch fee.

Repayment caps at entireDebt minus minimum debt; it can repay less than requested. Entire debt includes accrued interest, batch management fees and redistribution. Zombie adjustment requires zombie status, sufficient resulting minimum debt and valid hints to reinsert. Normal operations enforce current oracle liveness, individual/system collateral constraints and branch shutdown status; close remains possible after shutdown. No shutdown, oracle-failure or permissionless maintenance method is admitted.

Nerite-specific branch debt-limit checks apply on opening and debt increases; source constants include 75% stability-pool yield allocation and 0.55% redemption floor, not a generic Liquity interface substitution. WETH constants declare CCR 150%, MCR/SCR 110%, BCR 10%, but constructor reads registry parameters; constants are not asserted as live immutable values without state evidence. Governance-controlled debt limits and price dependencies can block borrowing.

claimCollateral pays only caller surplus previously recorded by the CollSurplusPool; it is not unrestricted collateral withdrawal. Fee arithmetic truncates integer divisions, and financial parameters/hints/receiver/owner/manager choices remain caller responsibilities. No deadline, collateral output minimum or automatic financial validation is added.

functions.label: D2 Finance deposit
warnings: Static exact-deployment source/ABI inventory only; no fresh RPC/runtime identity, successful execution, funding, rate or financial-safety guarantee. Existing grants, canonical calldata/value checks, pauses and independent controls remain mandatory. All admitted methods require zero native value.

Arbitrum42161 direct nonproxy VaultV1Whitelisted 0x75288264FDFEA8ce68e6D852696aB1cE2f3E5004. Underlying is native USDC 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 (6decimals), not USDC.e or native ETH. Shares also use6decimals. Constructor name/symbol HYPE++ is current registry Alpha Strategies branding, not a separate new protocol.

All four ordinary methods require whitelisted[msg.sender] OR strictly more than whitelistBalance of mutable whitelistAsset. This gates callers, including smart accounts/operators, even withdrawals; the catalog cannot grant eligibility. Constructor whitelist token/threshold are not asserted current. Owner can change whitelist, whitelistAsset, whitelistBalance and maxDeposits.

Deposit/mint pull USDC from caller using allowance to vault and mint shares to receiver. Only fundingStart <= now < epochStart and not custodied permit entry; current registry reports Trading and custodied=true, so admission does not imply calls are presently executable. Deposit/mint caps use totalDeposits versus maxDeposits, not simply vault cash.

Withdraw/redeem require not custodied and outside trading interval; caller must own shares or have existing share allowance from owner. No asynchronous request/cancel/claim queue exists in this implementation. If trader has custody, even scheduled epoch end does not unlock cash; trader must return funds and clear custodied. returnFunds can end epoch early and realize losses. No guaranteed redemption date; docs mention possible unwinding beyond expiry.

Immutable trader 0x8cABD8b787E8c69c5F24091CFdA197ff570345B3 can take whole vault assets for strategy execution during epoch. While custodied, totalAssets reports historical custodiedAmount, not live marked-to-market strategy NAV. Trader return amount may be lower. Owner schedules epochs (up to3650days) and capacity; source has no separate pause variable but custody/funding/whitelist gates can block operations.

ERC4626 virtual+1 conversion with decimal offset0: deposits/redeems round down; mint/withdraw round up. No caller-set minShares/minAssets/maxAssets/deadline exists. No explicit user fee deduction in this vault source; external strategy performance fees and accounting can affect returned NAV. Current official strategy guide gives HYPE++ example0% management/20% performance, not an immutable vault fee or current setting attestation. Rebasing/transfer-tax assets unsupported by source.

Current primary GitBook links production strategies and describes active V1/V3 vaults; official HYPE++ article supports Arbitrum access. Exact current Alpha Strategies/USDC target and Trading epoch23 metadata were retrieved from official staging.d2.finance API (not production response). Production/app/docs requests and browser hit Cloudflare. Staging also lists tests, so only independently exact-mainnet-source-bound Arbitrum target is selected; no test/staging-chain deployment is admitted.

Official terms restrict participation to legally eligible high-net-worth/sophisticated investors and prohibit listed territories including US,UK,Australia,China,HongKong,Switzerland and sanctioned jurisdictions, plus geographical masking. Contract whitelist is not legal eligibility. Managed strategy can use V0 Porto policy-engine custody; this inventory admits only the exact user vault interface, not trader/OMS/bridge/custody execution.

warnings: Static exact-deployment ABI/source inventory only; no runtime identity, execution, liquidity, funding, complete-workflow or financial-safety assurance. Independent grants, pause checks and canonical-calldata controls remain mandatory.

Deposit transfers caller USDC into this vault using allowance to this vault, then forwards a request to its configured aggregate vault. Redeem escrows owner shares in this vault rather than immediately burning/paying them. minOutAfterFees is forwarded into the pending request without local enforcement. Bundled aggregate source stores it for deferred execution; current exact aggregate/request-handler source and minimum-enforcement implementation were not independently bound, and no live execution/min-output guarantee is asserted. No caller deadline is present.

Conversions floor at the share price and dynamic fees can consume small inputs; deposit requires nonzero preview shares and capacity, redeem requires nonzero preview assets and sufficient aggregate USDC before it can even queue. Documented fees are 2% annual management and 20% yield plus dynamic entry/exit fees; actual configured execution-time rates may differ.

Requests depend on keeper/oracle execution, configured hooks, buffers and rebalancing; no fixed settlement delay or payout guarantee. cancelRequest checks exact vault and initiating sender, returns escrowed USDC or shares and clears the pending request; already cleared/executed or unavailable escrow requests can revert, and keeper ETH is not refunded by this function.

Explorer snapshot reports depositPaused=false, withdrawalPaused=false, aggregateVault=0x1E914730B4Cd343aE14530F0BBF6b350d83B833d and asset=USDC. These are point-in-time reported values, not persistence or runtime attestation. Configurator can pause operations or replace aggregateVault; the immutable AUTH reference is not automatically replaced with it.

Caller-selected callback variants, permit, approvals/transfers, privileged share accounting, pause/configuration and all views are excluded. The fixed configured aggregate dependency may revert or change; its source bundled in the vault compilation is contextual only, not an independently verified current deployed aggregate ABI. Umami requires lawful jurisdictional participation; no KYC eligibility or legal suitability is inferred.

functions.label: Sumer borrow usdc
warnings: Static deployment/source/ABI inventory only: not proof of current runtime identity, execution, liquidity, funding, backing, financial safety or complete workflow. Independent grants, pauses, canonical calldata and value policies remain mandatory.

Arbitrum One 42161 sdrUSDC proxy 0x4DE3741E1676ed14d661b1398196dC221cA4D37A uses six-decimal native USDC 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831; receipt sdrUSDC also has six decimals. This is Sumer own lending market, not synthetic-token issuer, bridge, or a generic Compound ABI. Selected calls are nonpayable with zero native value.

mint transfers caller USDC atomically using allowance to sdrUSDC proxy and credits caller receipts; actual transferred amount must exceed 1000 USDC base units (0.001 USDC) and minted receipt amount must be nonzero. Source controller auto-enters collateral membership on first clean deposit, and enforces market listing, mint pause, exchange-rate bound and supply cap; documentation no-minimum statement is superseded by exact deployed source.

redeem takes receipt base units; redeemUnderlying takes exact USDC base units. Exchange-rate multiplication/division floors. Unless redeeming the entire receipt balance, both burned receipts and underlying amount must exceed 1000 respective base units, and a remaining receipt balance of 1..1000 is rejected. Caller health, controller checks and market cash still apply. No slippage/deadline input exists.

borrow creates caller debt; controller checks listed markets, existing market pause states, borrow caps and collateral shortfall. repayBorrow and repayBorrowBehalf pull caller USDC using existing allowance, capped at borrower outstanding debt; third-party repayment does not grant borrowing delegation. Interest accrual, reserve factor and exchange-rate rounding remain material; no standalone prefunding or approval capability is admitted.

Borrow and redemption attempt configured timelock.consumeValue(amount). If that low-level call fails, the market transfers USDC to configured Timelock atomically and creates an agreement for caller instead of immediate payout. The timelock address is controller-configured, not a caller-selected executor. A failed dependency may still revert the entire call; no immediate receipt or payout assurance.

Timelock claim(uint256[]) can claim any recorded caller-beneficiary agreement, not only USDC agreements. Beneficiary must equal msg.sender; global and per-agreement freeze checks apply. Maturity requires timestamp + minDelay < current timestamp; before maxDelay the rate limiter must allow consumption, after maxDelay its reset-capable path is used. ERC20 output goes to recorded beneficiary; native agreements use a 5300-gas payment to that same beneficiary. No arbitrary target, recipient, calldata or bridge route input is admitted.

Explorer observation reports market isDeprecated=false, symbol=sdrUSDC, decimals=6 and underlying as above. isCTokenDeprecated=true is a deprecated storage classification flag, NOT the separate isDeprecated() market lifecycle result. Timelock frozen=false, minDelay=300 seconds and maxDelay=43200 seconds at observation only; mutable roles, upgrades, limiter state, agreements and balances may change or prevent claims.

Official current app vendor bundle binds arbitrum deployment addresses and token pair; main app maps networkId 42161 to nameInCompoundjs arbitrum. Sourcify reports exact_match for market, controller and timelock proxies and resolved implementations, not independent runtime persistence. Controller dependency is reviewed but its direct entrypoints are not admitted; no other markets or suToken issuer roles gain capabilities. Legal/KYC/jurisdiction eligibility is not established by this source inventory.

functions.label: Stryke Buy current WETH/USDC fixed-expiry option
warnings: Static deployment-bound source/ABI metadata only: not runtime attestation, live funding/liquidity, financial safety, execution or complete-workflow assurance. Canonical Stryke includes the Dopex rebrand once. Only the current Arbitrum WETH/USDC OptionMarketOTMFE 0x2536974545c28F7C7d17038c7623E8132FbD82bb is admitted; official docs separately mark old Arbitrum/Base deployments deprecated. The market, current PositionManager 0x467f2E854C53DFC44e592600c4E0E9e86898E84b and UniswapV3Handler 0x6F73aFB6598d7a3881577f884f2E01574aEFC373 are direct contracts, not proxies; source service labels all match, not exact_match.

mintOption requires approvedMinters[msg.sender]; catalog membership cannot supply that eligibility. At most 20 ticks, approved pool/hook/TTL, minimum liquidity, configured strike bounds/max tick width and out-of-money checks apply. TTL is a fixed-expiry grid anchored at ttlStartTime, not simply now+ttl; BUFFER_TIME excludes the beginning of the grid cycle. No permissionless eligibility, app access, KYC/jurisdiction clearance or future availability is asserted.

For calls the caller pays WETH 0x82af49447d8a07e3bd95bd0d56f35241523fbab1; for puts the caller pays USDC 0xaf88d065e77c8cc2239327c5edb3a432268e5831. Amounts are token base units. safeTransferFrom pulls premium into the market and any fee directly to feeTo using caller allowance to this market; maxCostAllowance caps premium plus protocol fee. There is no payable ETH conversion. Floor allocation can leave premium dust in market.

Typed optionTicks choose handler/pool/hook, not arbitrary selector or bytes. Market builds fixed use/donate payloads to its immutable PositionManager; manager requires approved handler/app pairing, and handler has its own app whitelist/pause. Registered hook callbacks, pricing, fee and verified-spot dependencies can be configured by governance; approved settings and external hook behavior are not continuously attested or isolated by this metadata.

positionSplitter requires the actual NFT owner msg.sender (approved operators cannot substitute), an unexpired option and exact liquidityToSplit array length. It deducts each split from original liquidity and mints a new option with the same expiry/strike/type to to; no ERC20 payout or extension results. Recipient must be intentional and contracts must accept safeMint ERC721 receipt. Subtraction bounds apply; no promise that a split is immediately exercisable.

settleOption is deliberately excluded: settler-role gated and takes dynamic swapper addresses plus opaque swapData, may pay profits to settler rather than NFT owner. Current LP mint/burn/reserve methods through PositionManager are also excluded because dynamic handler plus opaque hook-bearing bytes require scoped execution not provided here. Handler addLiquidity is not a substitute: it directly mints raw Uniswap liquidity to recipient without ERC6909 share bookkeeping and does not enforce its amountMin fields. No callback, arbitrary multicall, approval, raw prefunding or complete exit workflow is admitted.

deposit pulls computed token0/token1 amounts from msg.sender directly into this vault using vault allowances and mints shares to intentional recipient to. withdraw burns only msg.sender shares without a delegated-owner allowance route, then proportionally removes configured pool positions, collects fees and transfers both tokens to to. Desired deposit amounts cap source-computed token usage; shares round down while proportional token inputs round up. For an empty vault, shares equal max(amount0Desired,amount1Desired) in raw base units, not normalized USD value. Withdrawal proportional liquidity and amounts round down; tiny withdrawals may burn too little position liquidity and differ from previews.

User value includes idle vault assets and concentrated-liquidity positions, net of accrued protocol/strategist fees. Source TOTAL_FEE=1500/10000 takes 15% of collected pool trading fees, allocated 6667/10000 of that cut to Steer and the rest strategist; it is not a 15% principal entry/exit fee. Pool trading fees, impermanent loss, strategy positions/rebalances and integer rounding affect outcomes. Deposited tokens remain idle until a later manager rebalance, which is not admitted or guaranteed.

Amount-preserving standard WETH/USDC.e semantics are expected; transfer-tax/rebase/restricted tokens are not supported by the nominal accounting assumptions.

Point-in-time read-only configuration reports paused=false and registry state 1 (PendingThreshold), not Active=3; deposit source explicitly accepts either. This is a maintained officially listed pool, not a claim that strategy thresholds are met, liquidity is deployed, or calls will execute. functions.label: Hegic Claim position USDC.e profit
warnings: Static source/ABI metadata only, not assurance of current runtime identity, balances, liquidity, safety, successful execution or a complete workflow. Independent grants, pauses, canonical calldata and value controls remain required. All selected functions are nonpayable and require zero native value.

Exact Arbitrum Herge Stake & Cover pool, not legacy Ethereum V1/V8888 pools. HEGIC 0x431402e8b9de9aa016c743880e04e517074d8cec is cover collateral and USDC.e 0xff970a61a04b1ca14834a43f5de4533ebddb5cc8 is profit/payout token. Both are ERC20 token-base-unit amounts, not native ETH; native ETH only pays network gas separately.

provide pulls HEGIC from msg.sender using pool allowance. positionId=0 mints a new position NFT to msg.sender; an existing ID requires NFT ownership or approval, and funds accrue to that NFT owner. The first-ever position is admin-only. Entry is allowed only while now-epoch.start < mutable windowSize (source default 5 days); docs/UI mention 7 days, so do not assume that prose is current configuration.

provide floors amount*totalShare/coverTokenTotal (or uses amount when pool balance is zero), has no minimum shares or deadline, and can round small deposits to zero shares. It buffers accrued USDC.e profit before changing shares. HEGIC collateral can be spent to cover options losses; profit is neither fixed nor guaranteed.

withdraw is an asynchronous request, NOT a token payout: owner/approved caller specifies requested HEGIC amount, ceil-rounded shares are removed from position and queued in current epoch while totalShare remains until settlement. Final token amount depends on epoch-end remaining collateral; no fixed redemption price or immediate exit guarantee.

claim is permissionless but sends only this position's buffered USDC.e profit to ownerOf(positionId), never to caller-selected recipient. Profit uses cumulative floor rounding and admin fixProfit accounting, not an independent payout guarantee.

withdrawEpoch is permissionless but transfers final queued HEGIC and USDC.e only to current NFT owner. outFrom must contain completed epoch IDs with valid totalShareOut; current/future epochs revert, duplicates produce no additional entitlement, and zero-denominator epochs may revert. Pending profit is buffered then settled atomically; unwithdrawn collateral accounting is reduced. NFT transfer changes ultimate payout ownership.

Epoch closing is administered through fixProfit after strictly more than 7 days; permissionless fallbackEpochClose exists only after strictly more than 90 days and is not admitted as a trading capability. App mentions 30/45-day epochs and automatic withdrawals, but selected source requires explicit completed-epoch withdrawal; no exact timing or keeper promise.

Admin can alter entry window, payoffPool and next-epoch HEGIC conversion price and account/distribute realized profits; separately privileged treasury can exchange HEGIC for USDC.e through configured payoffPool allowance. This is economically shared options-writing exposure, not an isolated vault. No investor KYC/whitelist check appears on these entrypoints; no legal/app eligibility clearance is implied.

It buffers accrued USDC.e profit before changing shares. HEGIC collateral can be spent to cover options losses; profit is neither fixed nor guaranteed.

withdraw is an asynchronous request, NOT a token payout: owner/approved caller specifies requested HEGIC amount, ceil-rounded shares are removed from position and queued in current epoch while totalShare remains until settlement. Final token amount depends on epoch-end remaining collateral; no fixed redemption price or immediate exit guarantee.

claim is permissionless but sends only this position's buffered USDC.e profit to ownerOf(positionId), never to caller-selected recipient. Profit uses cumulative floor rounding and admin fixProfit accounting, not an independent payout guarantee.

withdrawEpoch is permissionless but transfers final queued HEGIC and USDC.e only to current NFT owner. outFrom must contain completed epoch IDs with valid totalShareOut; current/future epochs revert, duplicates produce no additional entitlement, and zero-denominator epochs may revert. Pending profit is buffered then settled atomically; unwithdrawn collateral accounting is reduced. NFT transfer changes ultimate payout ownership.

Epoch closing is administered through fixProfit after strictly more than 7 days; permissionless fallbackEpochClose exists only after strictly more than 90 days and is not admitted as a trading capability. App mentions 30/45-day epochs and automatic withdrawals, but selected source requires explicit completed-epoch withdrawal; no exact timing or keeper promise.

Admin can alter entry window, payoffPool and next-epoch HEGIC conversion price and account/distribute realized profits; separately privileged treasury can exchange HEGIC for USDC.e through configured payoffPool allowance. This is economically shared options-writing exposure, not an isolated vault. No investor KYC/whitelist check appears on these entrypoints; no legal/app eligibility clearance is implied.

unlock is permissionless after strictly now > expiration and releases only treasury accounting, with no wallet payout. It cannot be used to claim expired-option value; an option must be exercised before expiry if applicable. Repeated settlement reverts through Locked state checks.

Treasury may call immutable CoverPool to replenish USDC.e from its configured payoffPool when needed. Admin treasury withdrawals/configuration and stake collateral conversion remain explicit economic dependencies, not safety assurances.

functions.label: Ramses V3 swap exact input single
warnings: Static deployment/source/ABI metadata only; no persistent runtime attestation, live grants, liquidity, funding, financial safety, route coverage or successful-execution assurance. Independent policies, grants, pauses and canonical calldata/value checks remain mandatory.

This is Ramses current Arbitrum V3 concentrated-liquidity SwapRouter 0x4730e03EB4a58A5e20244062D5f9A99bCf5770a6 published in current primary deployment docs, NOT excluded retired Ramses V1 or the separately labeled Legacy V2 router. No unsupported HyperEVM/Robinhood chain, OFT transfer or token-migration scope is added. The deployed router is nonproxy; full deployment-bound matching source and original ABI are retained.

Only exactInputSingle and exactOutputSingle are admitted. Their tuple supplies tokenIn/tokenOut, signed int24 tickSpacing, recipient, deadline, input/output quantity bound and sqrtPriceLimitX96. These are fixed financial swap parameters, not a caller-selected execution target, selector or arbitrary command. Source computes the pool deterministically using immutable deployer, sorted tokens, tickSpacing and fixed init-code hash; callback verifies sender against that derived pool. Direct callback, multicall, UniversalRouter commands, permits, sweeps and refunds remain excluded.

Current explorer immutable getters identify WETH9=0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 and pool deployer=0xb722efaAbe807FAeA16068f595EaA9aa1a62CECD, matching the current primary registry. Valid token pairs/tick spacing require a deployed supported pool and suitable liquidity. This snapshot does not inventory or attest every pool, token, oracle, factory role or future market configuration.

Caller is fixed as payer. ERC20 input is pulled from msg.sender by router allowance in validated pool callback; no raw pool prefunding or standalone mint/burn is used. For WETH9 input the payment routine first uses any native ETH already held by router, wrapping only amount owed, then otherwise pulls WETH. For ordinary token-funded swaps send zero native value and pre-establish needed input allowance. Catalog adds no approval/signature authority.

Both selected ABI methods are payable but do not automatically refund unused ETH, unwrap WETH output or sweep assets. Native-funded exact-output swaps and nonzero price-limit partial fills can leave ETH/input residue publicly recoverable through excluded refund/sweep methods. Do not overpay, prefund router, set recipient=zero/router, or assume a complete native-asset workflow; route output directly to intended nonzero recipient. Zero recipient deliberately redirects output into router custody. Token output to third parties is intentional recipient authority, not own-wallet protection.

exactInputSingle requests amountIn and enforces amountOut>=amountOutMinimum. A nonzero sqrtPriceLimitX96 can produce a partial input fill. exactOutputSingle enforces amountIn<=amountInMaximum; when sqrtPriceLimitX96=0 source also requires full amountOut, while a nonzero limit explicitly permits receiving less than requested output. Set limits intentionally; return values are respectively output received and input paid. No fee-on-transfer/rebasing-token compatibility or receiver delta guarantee is asserted.

Quantity fields use each token base units, deadline uses Unix seconds with block.timestamp<=deadline, sqrtPriceLimitX96 uses Q64.96, and tickSpacing is NOT a fee basis-point field. Zero price limit selects near-extreme allowed V3 price boundary. Pool swap math determines price impact, rounding and fees; use meaningful minimum-output/maximum-input, deadline and optional directional price bound. No fixed rate or fee is promised.

Current primary docs distinguish V3 AMM from Legacy V2 and identify Arbitrum as DEX-only, separate from token OFT connectivity. This does not restore retired V1 deployments. Packed multihop path methods are separately inventoried but not admitted in this explicitly typed single-pool scope; no claim they are arbitrary executable calldata is made.

functions.label: Ostium cancelRequestDeposit own USDC/OLP request
warnings: Static deployment/source/ABI metadata only, not live authorization, persistent runtime attestation, liquidity, capital safety, successful execution or complete workflow. Independent grants, pauses and canonical calldata/value controls remain mandatory; nonpayable calls require zero native value.

Arbitrum current OstiumVault proxy 0x20d419a8e12c45f88fda7c5760bb6923cee27f98 resolves to implementation 0xacff332d0d8c34162be6bbabf7d676fea7cd0f3e, with exact_match runtime/creation source records. Current primary docs separately document request-and-settle deposits/withdrawals. Historical direct ERC4626 deposit/mint/withdraw/redeem functions unconditionally revert and are excluded; legacy locked-position unlock is excluded.

All admitted request/cancel/claim/reclaim records are msg.sender-owned; no user-selected receiver, executor, calldata, signature, admin or delegation power. requestDeposit pulls caller native Arbitrum USDC; requestWithdraw transfers caller OLP into vault custody. USDC and OLP use 6 decimals. Positive amounts required for requests/cancellations; native value is zero.

Requests target lastSettlementId+1 for deposits and lastSettlementId+1+withdrawSettlementDelay for withdrawals. Settlement timing and delay are mutable; docs describe typical daily/2-3-day behavior, not a guaranteed deadline. Observed delay was 2 settlements. Settlement depends on protocol/MM/oracle state and may be delayed; this admission does not grant settlement/MM/operator methods.

Deposit cap allocation is pro rata when requests exceed available capacity; claimDeposit floors allocated assets and shares at settlement price, transfers caller assigned OLP and refunds unallocated USDC. If no deposit capacity exists the request becomes reclaimable rather than minting shares. No caller minimum shares or price bound is provided.

If total requested withdrawal shares exceed settlement balance/share limits, that settlement batch is made reclaimable; otherwise conversion uses recorded settlement price with floor rounding. claimWithdraw clears caller request and returns USDC, while reclaimWithdraw returns caller OLP after rejected batch. These reclaim methods handle ordinary current request rejection, not hacked/frozen legacy recovery.

Pending cancellation may reduce an own request before settlement and returns its assets/shares. Once claimable or reclaimable, the whole recorded amount is claimed/reclaimed and state cleared before token transfer. OLP is exposed to trader PnL, buffer depletion, mutable collateralization and liquidity constraints; neither pricing nor principal protection is assured.

Historical direct ERC4626 deposit/mint/withdraw/redeem functions unconditionally revert and are excluded; legacy locked-position unlock is excluded.

All admitted request/cancel/claim/reclaim records are msg.sender-owned; no user-selected receiver, executor, calldata, signature, admin or delegation power. requestDeposit pulls caller native Arbitrum USDC; requestWithdraw transfers caller OLP into vault custody. USDC and OLP use 6 decimals. Positive amounts required for requests/cancellations; native value is zero.

Requests target lastSettlementId+1 for deposits and lastSettlementId+1+withdrawSettlementDelay for withdrawals. Settlement timing and delay are mutable; docs describe typical daily/2-3-day behavior, not a guaranteed deadline. Observed delay was 2 settlements. Settlement depends on protocol/MM/oracle state and may be delayed; this admission does not grant settlement/MM/operator methods.

Deposit cap allocation is pro rata when requests exceed available capacity; claimDeposit floors allocated assets and shares at settlement price, transfers caller assigned OLP and refunds unallocated USDC. If no deposit capacity exists the request becomes reclaimable rather than minting shares. No caller minimum shares or price bound is provided.

If total requested withdrawal shares exceed settlement balance/share limits, that settlement batch is made reclaimable; otherwise conversion uses recorded settlement price with floor rounding. claimWithdraw clears caller request and returns USDC, while reclaimWithdraw returns caller OLP after rejected batch. These reclaim methods handle ordinary current request rejection, not hacked/frozen legacy recovery.

Pending cancellation may reduce an own request before settlement and returns its assets/shares. Once claimable or reclaimable, the whole recorded amount is claimed/reclaimed and state cleared before token transfer. OLP is exposed to trader PnL, buffer depletion, mutable collateralization and liquidity constraints; neither pricing nor principal protection is assured.

lendGivenPrincipal derives funding payer from msg.sender and internally constructs callback data; no caller-supplied bytes, arbitrary executor, route, delegatecall or backend signature is accepted by this selected ABI. Fixed callbacks verify the expected immutable factory-derived pool/option or fixed position-token caller. Callbacks, multicall and generic native-balance refund/unwrap helpers remain excluded. No new contract-wallet execution/signing scope is introduced.

Lending supplies one configured pair asset in native token units, and mints ERC1155 Short lending position to param.to. token0/token1 must identify a valid factory pair; they are financial asset identifiers, not arbitrary call targets. Strike is a Q128 ratio; maturity and deadline are Unix seconds. Base-denomination conversion floors in this path and position units depend on strike/pair denomination, not a universal 18-decimal share unit. minReturnAmount and deadline are enforced after/before operation atomically.

Payable lender supports existing native-value model only: if selected funding asset is immutable wrapped native and router native balance covers payment, pay wraps it then transfers fixed amount to option pair; otherwise it pulls caller ERC20 using existing allowance. Shared router native balance can be consumed by this branch; do not prefund/rely on public residual balances. Supply exact necessary native value for native funding or zero for ERC20 funding. Excess/incorrect native value is not refunded by lendGivenPrincipal and public refundNatives is deliberately not admitted; native value is not universally zero for this payable method.

withdraw transfers only msg.sender ERC1155 Short position through existing position-token authorization into withdrawer, burns it, and collects matured option assets to param.to. No operator authorization is granted here. Both token output minima and deadline are checked atomically. It returns token0 and/or token1 ERC20 assets; choose recipient that can receive both. Set nonpayable withdrawal native value to zero. Unwrap-to-native shared-balance helper is excluded.

Maturity settlement is not principal protection: borrower default can produce collateral/alternate-asset payout instead of original principal, and principal value can fall. AMM price/interest and core market fee/rounding effects determine positions and proceeds; periphery selected bodies add no separate fee parameter. Factory validity and source binding do not certify any pair asset, reserves, liquidity, maturity availability or payout value. No early-close, full lending/borrowing workflow, automatic conversion, backing or yield assurance is promised.

warnings: Static deployment/source/ABI metadata only; not live authorization, persistent runtime attestation, liquidity, backing, financial safety, successful execution or a complete workflow. Single current Rain production Arbitrum order-book market diamond 0x21a1de432ca1107c3a0f308aeb024abc487575d1 only (Liverpool vs Brighton; option IDs 1 Liverpool, 2 Brighton, 3 Draw; side 1 YES/2 NO). Current primary API marked Live and FACTORY() returned official production factory 0x38b3ba1ee001e6785224e31b3031ae96ca06c677. This is ordinary prediction accounting, not a bridge, governance or token router. Market settlement/expiry is not a claim that the protocol is winding down.

Diamond root has exact_match creation/runtime source records; direct facets() captured all 10 current facet addresses and selector routes. Nine facet source snapshots retain Sourcify runtimeMatch=match (not exact_match); no stronger runtime identity is asserted. Read-only loupe implementation 0x514a99305711914c32c4d4a6ea9f2cb60475c643 has no obtainable Sourcify source (404); its exact routed interface is inventoried from IDiamondLoupe in the preserved financial facet sources. Owner/factory upgrades remain material.

Pool tradingModel() is OrderBook=1, so enterLiquidity, enterLiquidityBatch and removeLiquidity are structurally inapplicable and excluded even though routed. No AMM liquidity capability, arbitrary executor, user-programmable callback, wallet authorization, permit, role mutation or new off-chain signing capability is admitted.

USD₮0 base token 0xfd086bc7cd5c481dcc9c85ebe478a1c0b69fcbb9 uses 6 decimals; baseTokenDecimals() returns scale factor 1000000, not the integer decimal count. Outcome shares are internal accounting in base-unit scale, not transferable ERC20 tokens. Order prices are 1e18-scaled with configured tick/range rules; integer divisions floor fills, fees and payouts.

enterOption and placeBuyOrder pull only msg.sender approved base funds; order fills credit caller internal outcome shares. enterOption uses minSharesOut and deadline and refunds unfilled base; sellOption sells only caller unescrowed shares and enforces net-base minAmountOut and deadline. Partial sells leave unfilled shares with caller. These methods match only fixed on-chain order data, not opaque API calldata.

placeBuyOrder/placeSellOrder use a finite option/side/price/amount/postOnly interface. Resting buy orders escrow caller base; sell orders escrow only caller existing outcome shares. postOnly rejects crossing orders; otherwise matching and partial fills can occur before a remainder rests. Orders have no caller deadline or separate slippage bound beyond limit price. There are configured entry/dust minima, 50 active-order limits and maker rebates/protocol fees. Small base remainders are refunded; small share remainders remain available. Gas can grow with traversed book depth.

cancelBuyOrders/cancelSellOrders require each order maker to equal msg.sender and parallel arrays to match; cancellation returns only remaining own base escrow or releases own share escrow. It remains possible after trading phases, so existing escrow can be cleared before claim; races with fills can invalidate orders.

split pulls caller collateral and creates equal YES/NO internal shares; merge consumes equal caller unescrowed YES/NO shares and returns same-unit base. Both operate only before permanent option finalization and reject zero. No shared raw pool prefunding or public-mint workaround is used.

claim is caller-specific, one-time, after option finalization and dispute window. It requires no outstanding caller order escrow and pays pro-rata winning direct/LP shares and fees, with floor rounding; losing positions may receive zero and be ineligible. The first claim also settles fixed creator/platform/resolver/referrer/dispute/bond recipients and may invoke configured appeal-oracle refund. User cannot choose arbitrary targets or executable data. There is no payout minimum or guaranteed settlement date; resolver/oracle decisions can affect outcomes.

Money-moving methods use an accounted balance-delta hook whose ledger address is read from factory.accounting(); ledger authorization, mutable solvency gates or a dependency revert can block operations.
